Sports.title: Joshua-Fury Needs Promotion as Dana White and Eddie Hearn Bicker
Sports.content:
Dana White now describes himself as one of the promoters of Anthony Joshua’s December 11 fight with Tyson Fury, saying that his team will produce the event that night.

White’s latest comments put him alongside Eddie Hearn and Frank Warren in his description of the operation, although his clearest commitment concerns production.

“I’m producing the fight. Me and my team will be producing the fight that night. And I guess we’ll call me one of the promoters of the event because you do have Frank Warren and Eddie Hearn that are both promoters too, promoting the event,” White told BBC 5 Live.

The heavyweight fight is scheduled for Cardiff’s Principality Stadium. White also credited Hearn with securing the UK location during his interview with Steve Bunce.

The wording deserves attention. “I guess we’ll call me” sounds like White describing how he sees his involvement rather than announcing a newly agreed contractual position. It leaves the formal promotional arrangements unresolved, but makes clear that he expects a substantial role when the fighters enter the ring.

White and Hearn’s continuing argument over their roles is becoming tiresome. Every interview spent discussing who gets to call himself a promoter is another opportunity lost to explain why Joshua-Fury is still worth watching in December.

The names are familiar, but that does not mean the fight sells itself. Many fans see Joshua and Fury as two former champions meeting years after the contest should have happened. The promotion needs to address that skepticism rather than assume their past achievements will be enough.

There is still a fight to sell: the rivalry, the contrasting styles and the consequences of defeat for both men. Fans want to know what Joshua and Fury have left and whether either can produce something better than their recent performances suggest.

White and Hearn arguing over credit gives those viewers little reason to get excited. They need to spend more time promoting the fighters and less time promoting their own involvement.

Sports.title: Floyd Schofield Camp Threatens Cancellation Over Bahdi Weight
Sports.content:
Floyd Schofield’s father is threatening to pull Saturday’s fight against Lucas Bahdi if the Canadian exceeds 146 pounds at the second-day weight check, according to Chris Mannix. Bahdi’s team disputes his account of the negotiations and insists its fighter will come in at 145 or below.

The disagreement emerged Friday night ahead of their vacant WBA lightweight title fight in Chicago. Mannix reports that Illinois requires fighters in championship bouts to come in within ten pounds of the contract weight at a second-day check. For a fight contracted at 135 pounds, that means a 145-pound limit.

Floyd Sr. claims Bahdi’s side tried to negotiate a 15-pound allowance, which would permit him to reach 150 pounds. He also alleges they offered an additional $250,000 for each extra pound Bahdi was allowed.

According to Floyd Sr., Schofield’s camp agreed to 146 pounds but would refuse to proceed if Bahdi came in any heavier.

A representative from Bahdi’s side called Schofield’s version “total bullshit” and told Mannix that Bahdi would come in at 145 pounds or less.

That leaves two different accounts of what happened behind the scenes. The alleged financial offer comes from Floyd Sr., and Bahdi’s representative denies his version. It cannot be treated as an accepted account of the negotiations.

There is also an unanswered question about the 146-pound allowance. That figure exceeds the Illinois limit Mannix describes by one pound. His report does not establish whether the commission approved an exception or whether Floyd Sr. was describing only an agreement between the camps.

For Schofield, the concern is how much weight Bahdi can regain before they enter the ring. His father has now attached a cancellation threat to that concern, putting additional pressure on Saturday’s check.

Bahdi’s side has given itself a clear number to meet. If he comes in at 145 pounds or below, he would satisfy both the reported state limit and Schofield Sr.’s stated demand. Anything above 146 would test whether Schofield’s camp follows through on its threat.

Sports.title: Foster Questions Shakur Stevenson’s Chances Against Devin Haney
Sports.content:
O’Shaquie Foster argues that Devin Haney presents a far trickier technical challenge for Shakur Stevenson than Teofimo Lopez ever did. In his view, Stevenson’s victory over Lopez fails to prove how he would manage Haney’s specific tools.

While Foster stopped short of outright picking Haney, his breakdown casts doubt on Stevenson’s ability to rely on his trademark patience. He sees a scenario where Stevenson must abandon his comfort zone to press the action against an opponent who scores effectively from range.

“I have yet to see Shakur deal with the reach and the long jab of an elite fighter, like an elite boxer that can think on the move like him, that can make adjustments,” Foster told Sean Zittel. “It’s going to be difficult.”

Foster based that comparison on a harsh critique of Teofimo. While acknowledging Lopez’s physical gifts, Foster slammed his ring generalship.

“He’s athletic. He uses that to his advantage, but his IQ is terrible,” Foster said.

That contrast forms the core of Foster’s argument. Wild bursts of athletic speed present entirely different problems than a disciplined jab fired from the outside by a composed boxer.

If Haney controls distance with that jab, Shakur risks falling behind on the scorecards while waiting for openings that never arrive. To win rounds, Stevenson would have to close the space, disrupt the timing, and initiate contact instead of waiting on mistakes.

Applying pressure brings real danger. Stevenson would need to slip through Haney’s reach without overextending or aimlessly following him across the canvas. Foster also noted that Haney might sit down on his punches if he respects Stevenson’s power less over time.

Foster also waved off old sparring clips as irrelevant ancient history.

Ultimately, Foster envisions a tactical duel where Stevenson must prove he can adapt to an opponent who matches his boxing brain from distance. For Foster, beating Lopez left those questions unanswered.

Sports.title: WBA World Title Bout Schofield vs Bahdi
Sports.content:
In the Golden Boy and Most Valuable Promotions (MVP) cross-promoted main event, a new champion will be crowned as Floyd Schofield will face Lucas Bahdi on Saturday night, October 10th, at the Wintrust Arena in Chicago, live on DAZN.

This matchup features two undefeated fighters who are both determined, hungry, and ready to take their careers to the next level. The winner of this highly anticipated lightweight fight will be awarded the vacant WBA world title.

Since signing with Golden Boy Promotions in August 2022, Floyd Schofield has made the transition from prospect to contender. In his most recent outing, a definitive statement was made as he stopped Tevin Farmer in the first round.

His October 10th opponent, Lucas Bahdi, didn’t have the luxury of being guided by a well-known promotional company. Bahdi was winning consistently, as he achieved most of his success under the radar.

Two years ago, Bahdi introduced himself to the mainstream when he knocked Ashton Sylve out cold in the sixth round. Now in a high-stakes matchup, Lucas “Prince” Bahdi (20-0, 15 KOs) is set to battle Floyd “Kid Austin” Schofield (19-0, 13 KOs).

Lucas Bahdi is a very patient fighter who is accurate, good at controlling range, has good timing, and has a powerful right hand. The fear for Bahdi is due to his economical punch output; he can get outworked and fall behind on the scorecards.

Floyd Schofield is athletic, has a solid jab, fast hands, throws a variety of combinations, and is a strong puncher. Schofield is a fast starter, but the question for Schofield is: can he sustain his energetic pace during the later rounds?

Now promoted by MVP, the Ontario, Canada native Lucas Bahdi knows a win on Saturday night will take his career to another level. Bahdi plans on representing and taking full advantage of the opportunity.

“I’m very proud to be Canadian. I wear that flag on my back when I enter the ring,” Bahdi said.”That was all part of the journey. Now here we are. We’re fighting for the world title and I’m ready.”

When the Austin, Texas product Floyd Schofield enters the ring on Saturday night, he will also be attempting to win his first world title. He appreciates the opportunity, and he appreciates the person that made it possible.

“This fight is for my pops. At the end of the day, he sacrificed his whole life for me just to be in this position. So I got a lot to prove Saturday,” Schofield said at the press conference.

On Saturday night, October 10th, the Schofield vs. Bahdi clash is guaranteed to be an action-packed event. Both men will enter the ring undefeated, but by the end of the night, somebody’s 0 has got to go.

Sports.title: Tex Cobb and Tyson Fury Keep Boxing Laughing
Sports.content:
Tyson Fury reminds me of Randall “Tex” Cobb for a reason that has little to do with championship belts. Both could make people laugh in a sport where the usual sales pitch involves threatening to knock somebody out.

With Fury preparing to face Anthony Joshua on December 11 at Cardiff’s Principality Stadium, there will be plenty of attention on what he has to say before the opening bell. His personality has long been part of the attraction.

Cobb had that same ability to hold an audience, although his humor often came at his own expense.

I remember watching him kick a heavy bag at Joe Frazier’s Broad Street gym in Philadelphia. He came from a kickboxing background, and seeing him at work offered a reminder that beneath the jokes was a tough, serious fighter.

His biggest boxing victory came in August 1980, when he stopped the feared Earnie Shavers in the eighth round. That win helped take Cobb toward a heavyweight title opportunity against Larry Holmes.

Holmes gave him a punishing beating over 15 rounds in November 1982. The bout helped prompt Howard Cosell to stop broadcasting professional boxing, rather than retire from broadcasting altogether. Cobb nevertheless found a way to turn his defeat into a punchline.

“Larry Holmes didn’t beat me. He just won the first fifteen rounds,” Cobb joked.

That line explains his appeal better than a list of opponents. Cobb could acknowledge a beating without asking anyone to feel sorry for him. His film and television work later gave that personality an audience beyond boxing.

Fury’s humor serves a different purpose. His teasing and boasting help sell fights and draw opponents into the conversation he wants to have. He has also achieved far more in the ring than Cobb, becoming heavyweight champion rather than remaining a contender.

Still, there are limits to what a personality can accomplish. Fury’s two defeats against Oleksandr Usyk cannot reasonably be blamed on his mouthing off. Usyk beat him through his work in the ring, where a clever remark offers no substitute for landing punches.

The connection between Cobb and Fury is their ability to give fans something to remember beyond a result. Cobb could lose badly and still leave people repeating his jokes. Fury can command attention long before he throws a punch.

Boxing needs skilled fighters, but its colorful characters give people another reason to follow them. Cobb understood that, and Fury has made it a large part of his career.

Sports.title: Deontay Wilder Accepts Offer for Jai Opetaia Fight
Sports.content:
Deontay Wilder’s side has agreed to terms for a heavyweight meeting with Jai Opetaia on the Tyson Fury versus Anthony Joshua undercard, per Dan Rafael. That step nudges an odd co-feature closer to reality, even if the bout still needs an official green light.

Wilder’s manager, Shelly Finkel, told Rafael that their team gave the okay and is simply waiting on final sanctioning. Finkel noted that discussions regarding an encounter with Murat Gassiev occurred as well.

The proposal is on the table, though nothing is finalized. Wilder against Opetaia sounds nearly as bizarre as the debunked rumors pairing Manny Pacquiao with Shakur Stevenson. The difference is that paper exists here, even if the competitive logic feels thin.

Wilder is 40 and nearing the end of his run. Opetaia is 31, an elite cruiserweight jumping up in weight to take on an opponent whose marquee value outstrips his current form. Nearly a decade separates them, placing both men in drastically different stages of their journeys.

Wilder’s regression is well documented. The trademark right hand is dangerous against anyone stepping up in size, yet that single equalizer cannot carry the entire promotion. Defeats to Joseph Parker and Zhilei Zhang proved how quiet his offense becomes whenever foes take away his ideal launching lane.

Opetaia would certainly benefit from the spotlight of a massive pay-per-view platform. Even so, taking down an aging Wilder will tell observers very little about his viability against the division’s genuine contenders.

That reality exposes the flaw in the matchup. Wilder offers star power plus puncher’s luck. Opetaia brings youth and sharpness, but he has to jump weight classes just to make the attraction fit. Placing the bout on the undercard gives organizers another famous belt holder to market. It also highlights the growing sense that the event relies on nostalgic star power past its prime.

Finkel agreeing to the bout advances the paperwork, but it does nothing to turn this into a sensible contest. Putting him in with Opetaia only deepens the old-timers circus feel to the event. Opetaia is in his prime, fast, southpaw, and disciplined enough to pick apart a stationary target. Wilder getting outboxed or stopped by a cruiserweight moving up will not legitimize Opetaia as a real heavyweight threat; it will simply confirm that Wilder is completely washed up.

Sports.title: Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua Targets $34 Million Gate
Sports.content:
Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua’s December 11 fight in Cardiff is projected to generate a $34 million gate, Dana White told Sky Sports, putting the delayed heavyweight showdown on course for a British boxing record.

The figure shows how much commercial appeal remains in a fight that fans wanted years ago. Fury and Joshua are meeting later in their careers, but the opportunity to finally see them settle their rivalry has persuaded ticket buyers to spend heavily.

“I don’t want to mis-speak here but we have this thing scaled for around $34 million,” White told Sky Sports.

Regular tickets for the Principality Stadium event ranged from £88.50 to £13,128, excluding VIP, hotel and travel packages. White said fewer than 700 tickets remained on Friday evening after more than half a million people joined the Ticketmaster queue.

Those prices are a major part of the story. Filling a stadium demonstrates demand, but generating a record gate requires fans to pay enough across the seating plan. The projected revenue suggests the promoters have found buyers willing to treat Fury-Joshua as a major occasion despite the long wait.

For both fighters, that is the benefit of spending years becoming familiar names beyond boxing’s regular audience. Their previous defeats have changed how fans assess them in the ring, yet neither needs an unbeaten record to sell this particular matchup.

The unanswered question of who wins between them remains valuable. Fans who have followed the arguments for years now have a date and a venue, and the ticket response suggests many still want to witness the answer in person.

A record gate would underline how much business Fury and Joshua can still do together. It would also give promoters reason to pursue a second meeting if the first fight produces enough action or controversy to keep buyers interested.

For now, the $34 million remains a projection. The final receipts will determine the record, but the reported sales already show that the years of delays have not exhausted demand for Fury-Joshua.

Sports.title: Janibek Alimkhanuly Meets Jacob Bank for Vacant WBO Title
Sports.content:
Janibek Alimkhanuly now has a direct path to a belt at 168 pounds after the WBO confirmed terms are set for him to battle Jacob Bank for their vacant crown. Moving up provides Janibek another world title crack, while testing how well his middleweight firepower carries into the super middleweight ranks.

“DONE DEAL. Alimkhanuly vs. Bank for the vacant WBO Super Middleweight World Title!” the WBO announced on X.

The fight is reportedly headed to Copenhagen in December, although the WBO has yet to confirm the date, venue, or broadcaster.

Janibek has the edge in championship experience, but he still has to prove himself at 168. Bank gets the chance to test him against a bigger opponent and turn his first world title shot into the biggest win of his career.

If Bank can take Janibek’s power and keep pressing him, the former middleweight champion could have a difficult night. Janibek will need his jab and timing to control the exchanges rather than let Bank force him into a physical fight.

Bank gets the chance to make Janibek fight for every inch in this division. Taking out a hardened former middleweight champion gives Bank immediate legitimacy, proving he did more than pick up an abandoned strap. A victory also pushes his name into the mix for major work at 168 pounds.

Securing Copenhagen hands Bank true home-soil advantages. Fighting in front of his own people helps move tickets and guarantees strong local backing, but roaring fans will not solve the tactical problems Janibek presents once the bell rings.

Hamzah Sheeraz vacated the WBO title rather than face Janibek in an ordered defense. That opened the door for Bank, who now has a chance to win the belt against a former unified middleweight champion.

The date and venue still await confirmation. For Janibek, the fight tests whether he can reproduce his middleweight success at 168. Bank gets the chance to disrupt those plans and establish himself as champion.

Ghana News.title: Star Oil paid GH¢2.7bn in taxes, levies in nine months of 2026
Ghana News.content:
Philip Tieku, CEO of Star Oil.

Oil Marketing firm, Star Oil, paid GH¢2.7 billion in taxes and levies to the State, covering its operations from January 2026 to September 2026.

According to the firm’s year-to-date performance report, these payments covered several levies and taxes paid over the past nine months in 2026.

Ghana News.title: Samson’s Take: The rule of law is cheaper before the bulldozer
Ghana News.content:
Law is cheaper before the bulldozer. Sometimes you give a harmless caution, and it gets the usual treatment: “You are doing politics.”

For what benefit to me, really? On 19th September, I cautioned against the plan to demolish the La Pleasure Beach. An exercise expected that Sunday did not proceed. The bulldozer stayed away for about two weeks.

And I know that my take here was responsible for the stalling of the demolition. I knew the lead national security officer involved was unhappy with my intervention. But my caution was neither political nor complicated.

I was not deciding who owned the land. I said simply: where rights and ownership are disputed, let the law and the courts speak before the bulldozer. Simply follow due process.

It reminded me of another caution I gave eight years ago, right here on the show. In 2018, plans were made to demolish state properties to make way for the National Cathedral. I warned, quote, “There is no need to build a cathedral on a foundation of lies.”

That was not a position against building a cathedral. It was a caution about proceeding when serious questions had been raised about the justification for demolishing relatively new state properties and the cost of replacing them elsewhere. Different controversy. Same instinct.

Before the state exercises enormous power in a manner that may be irreversible, simply be sure of the facts, the law and the consequences. That’s all.

About two weeks after my September caution, the bulldozers eventually moved into the La Pleasure Beach. And I have deliberately not spent the days since saying, “I told you so.” I have no property there.

I represent none of the competing interests. I have no personal interest in who ultimately establishes title. I was simply doing this job, my job.

My concern was what ought to be sound and proper in a society governed by laws. And now, the bulldozers have spoken.

The Senate says it requested National Security’s intervention because it considers the occupation unlawful and says it has a responsibility to protect valuable assets belonging ultimately to workers and pensioners.

Fine. Those asserting rights to the land say otherwise. We have heard them.

Let the competing documents, the evidence and the law determine who is right, not the bulldozer. Nobody needs a bulldozer to determine title to land. That doesn’t happen in a democracy.

That is what the court is there for. If you have to eject people, simply use due process. But now, we hear concerns from traditional authorities.

We hear the MP and the NDC party’s constituency leadership. There is an obvious political cost developing around the exercise. I’m shocked it was not foreseen.

And now, we hear about compensation. If compensation is lawfully due, by all means, compensate those entitled to it. But I hope we will also hear about accountability.

Because if an avoidable exercise results in compensation, litigation or eventually judgment debts, somebody must account for the decision that created that liability.

When I spoke first, I referred to the Polo Beach and the fact that they were in court with the same institutions that apparently gave National Security instructions. And National Security was actually also in court. And the lead person, Richard Jakpa, was also in court. And there was an injunction process that was pending.

I hope the answer is not simply to reach for the public purse in this compensation matter.

The taxpayer must not become the insurer of official impatience. Bulldoze today, compensate tomorrow, charge it to the taxpayer. Nobody answers. Move on.

That cannot be the normal order of governance. And this is bigger than La Pleasure Beach, SSNIT, National Security or any particular government.

It is bigger than any particular government. Governments change. Officials change. Political parties will change. State power remains.

And whenever that enormous power confronts genuinely disputed rights, restraint is not weakness.

Due process is not an inconvenience. Sometimes, it protects the citizens. Sometimes, it protects government from itself.

And sometimes, it protects the taxpayer from paying tomorrow for an avoidable decision made today.

That is why the rule of law is cheaper before the bulldozer than after it. Before the bulldozer, it requires patience, notice, documents, due process and, where necessary, a judge.

After the bulldozer, there may be compensation, litigation, judgment debts, political damage and taxpayer money.

Eight years ago, my caution was, “Don’t build a cathedral on a foundation of lies.”

On 19 September, my caution was, “Let the law and the courts speak before the bulldozer.”

Different controversies, same principle. I am not interested in saying, “I told you so.” I am interested in whether we learn.

Let the law speak first. Let the courts speak before the bulldozer. And that is my take.

Ghana News.title: GRA blames system failure for delay in issuing receipt over passenger’s customs duty
Ghana News.content:
The Ghana Revenue Authority (GRA) says a GH¢807.68 customs duty assessed on a passenger’s luggage at the Accra International Airport was duly accounted for, following allegations of extortion involving Customs officers.

In a statement dated October 9, 2026, the Authority said preliminary investigations into the incident involving Gifty Osei Bonsu found that a temporary system failure disrupted the payment process, preventing the immediate issuance of an official receipt.

According to the GRA, Ms Bonsu arrived in Ghana aboard Egypt Air on October 3 and was referred for further examination after her luggage was selected for inspection at the Red Channel in the airport’s Arrivals Hall.

The inspection uncovered 20 pairs of new women’s shoes, nine new women’s dresses, 18 new men’s shirts and four new wigs.

The Authority said Customs officers assessed GH¢807.68 in duty on the 20 pairs of shoes.

However, the Integrated Customs Management System (ICUMS) was temporarily unavailable, affecting the processing of the payment and the issuance of an official receipt.

The GRA said Ms Bonsu, who indicated that she had a flight to catch, deposited GH¢600 with the officers towards the payment. A friend later deposited another GH¢200, bringing the total amount to GH¢800.

According to the Authority, the system was restored after the passenger had left the airport, allowing the full assessed duty to be paid into its revenue account at Ecobank Ghana Limited on the same day. An official receipt was subsequently generated in Ms Bonsu’s name.

The GRA added that the Customs officers used their personal funds to cover the GH¢7.68 difference between the amount collected and the assessed duty.

“The Authority wishes to assure the public that the transaction was undertaken in good faith and that the assessed duty was duly accounted for,” the statement said.

The Authority, however, acknowledged the delay in providing the service and apologised to Ms Bonsu for the inconvenience caused.

It said alternative procedures had been introduced to facilitate passenger services during system interruptions, while a review of the standard operating procedures governing Customs officers’ engagement with travellers at the country’s ports of entry had also begun.

The review will focus on professional communication, transparency in duty assessment and collection, and proper documentation of transactions.

The GRA further disclosed that it was developing an improved passenger-facing process to provide clearer information on Customs requirements, the calculation and payment of duties, and the channels available to passengers seeking clarification, challenging assessments or lodging complaints.

Ghana News.title: Livestream: Newsfile discusses World Cup visa scandal, beach demolitions, education strikes, BRICS bid
Ghana News.content:
JoyNews’ flagship current affairs programme, Newsfile, is examining four major national issues that have dominated public discussion over the past week.

The discussions will focus on allegations surrounding Ghana’s 2026 FIFA World Cup visa arrangements, demolitions along the La Beach area, strikes disrupting education, and the country’s bid to join the BRICS economic bloc.

Livestream:

World Cup visa controversy: EOCO probe or cover-up?

The programme will examine allegations by the Minority in Parliament over Ghana’s visa arrangements connected to activities surrounding the 2026 FIFA World Cup.

At a press conference on Wednesday, October 7, the Ranking Member on Parliament’s Youth and Sports Committee, Vincent Ekow Assafuah, alleged that some individuals paid between US$7,000 and US$14,000 for visa processing.

The Minority also questioned the verification of personnel whose names were submitted by the Ghana Tourism Authority (GTA) and the National Sports Authority (NSA) to the US and Canadian embassies.

It alleged that only two of 50 names submitted by the GTA as media personnel were verified as professional media practitioners, while 15 of 102 names submitted by the NSA were verified as actual employees.

President John Dramani Mahama has asked former NSA Director-General Yaw Ampofo Ankrah to step aside, with Professor Emmanuel Osei Sarpong appointed acting Director-General.

The Ministry of Sports and Recreation has provided a chronology of its engagements, citing correspondence dated January 28, 2026, which it says shows that some arrangements connected to the World Cup fan experience predated its involvement.

The programme will examine the allegations, the responses from the institutions involved and calls for further investigation.

Beach demolitions: Who is accountable?

The second topic will focus on the demolition of structures along the La Beach area in Accra, including La Pleasure Beach and the Polo Beach Club near the Labadi Beach Hotel.

The Social Security and National Insurance Trust (SSNIT) has defended the operation, saying it sought the intervention of the National Security Council Secretariat over what it described as persistent unlawful occupation, encroachment and unauthorised activities on the beachfront adjoining the Labadi Beach Hotel and La Palm Royal Beach Hotel.

SSNIT said the two hotels formed part of its investment portfolio and were significant national hospitality and tourism assets that it had a responsibility to protect.

“These assets belong to the workers and pensioners of Ghana,” the Trust stated.

However, Deputy Chief of Staff Stan Dogbe said the operation was not part of the government’s flood mitigation exercise, explaining that it was conducted under National Security supervision at the request of the Labadi Beach Hotel.

The Ghana Journalists Association has also condemned alleged attacks on journalists covering the demolitions and given the Ghana Armed Forces two weeks to account for the actions of its personnel.

Newsfile will examine the circumstances surrounding the operation, questions of accountability and the concerns raised by affected parties.

https://6c5fd197d25de85d0ef35fabcae8edf4.safeframe.googlesyndication.com/safeframe/1-0-45/html/container.html

Education crisis: Two strikes, who pays the price?

The programme will also discuss the impact of strikes by pre-tertiary teachers and university administrators on Ghana’s education system.

The three pre-tertiary teacher unions — the Ghana National Association of Teachers (GNAT), the National Association of Graduate Teachers (NAGRAT) and the Pre-Tertiary Teachers Association of Ghana (PRETAG) — have been on strike since September 25 over delayed promotions, deprived-area allowances and negotiations on a new collective bargaining agreement.

A meeting between the Fair Wages and Salaries Commission and union leadership on Tuesday, October 6, ended without an agreement.

Education Minister Haruna Iddrisu has pledged that the salary grades of at least 51,000 promoted teachers will be validated and their arrears paid by October 16 through a supplementary intervention.

“If by October 30, your promotion arrears are not paid, then I will have no honour,” he stated.

Meanwhile, the Ghana Association of University Administrators (GAUA) has been on strike for more than two months, disrupting administrative services at public universities.

University of Ghana Pro-Vice-Chancellor Professor Gordon Awandare has warned that the academic calendar could collapse if the strike extends into the following week.

“The reality is that currently many of the systems are not working because they are managed by members of GAUA who are on strike,” he said.

The Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST) has also postponed its reopening indefinitely because of the strike.

The discussion will consider the unresolved grievances, the impact on students and the prospects for ending the industrial actions.

Ghana’s BRICS bid: What does it mean for national interest?

The fourth topic will examine Ghana’s formal application to join the BRICS economic bloc, announced by Foreign Affairs Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa.

The Minority in Parliament has called for an urgent briefing on the decision, seeking clarity on its geopolitical implications and potential consequences for Ghana’s national interests.

The Ranking Member on Parliament’s Foreign Affairs Committee, Samuel Abu Jinapor, has questioned why Ghana is seeking full membership rather than following Nigeria’s approach as a BRICS partner country.

“Why is it that we are not taking the path of Nigeria, which is a partner country of BRICS and not a full member?” he asked.

Mr Ablakwa has defended the application, arguing that membership could broaden Ghana’s development and diplomatic options.

“BRICS offers us that opportunity to have options in our development agenda. We value our traditional relationships, but we must have new friends,” he said.

India’s External Affairs Minister, Dr S. Jaishankar, has welcomed Ghana’s interest, while noting that an expansion decision requires consensus among existing BRICS members.

The panel will examine the potential opportunities and implications of the bid, including its relationship with Ghana’s existing international partnerships.

Newsfile, hosted by Samson Lardy Anyenini, is airing on Joy 99.7 FM, JoyNews and other platforms.

Ghana News.title: NC-PTAs welcomes end of teachers’ strike, urges parents to prepare children for Monday
Ghana News.content:
The National Council of Parent-Teacher Associations (NC-PTAs) Ghana has welcomed the decision by teacher unions to call off their strike, urging parents and guardians to prepare their children to return to school on Monday, October 12, 2026.

In a press statement dated October 10, the Council said it was pleased with the communiqué signed on October 9 between the government, represented by the Fair Wages and Salaries Commission (FWSC) and the Ghana Education Service (GES), and the teacher unions — the Ghana National Association of Teachers (GNAT), the National Association of Graduate Teachers (NAGRAT) and the Pre-Tertiary Teachers Association of Ghana (PRETAG).

The Council expressed gratitude to President John Dramani Mahama for his intervention, as well as the government’s negotiating team and teacher union leaders for reaching an agreement to end the industrial action.

“We are grateful that teachers have called off the strike to return to full classroom work on Monday, 12th October, 2026,” the statement, signed by the General Secretary, Gapson Kofi Raphael, said.

The NC-PTAs also thanked the unions for choosing dialogue over a prolonged dispute, acknowledging that teachers had raised concerns they considered important to their welfare.

It urged all parties to honour the commitments reached during negotiations, particularly those relating to outstanding promotion arrears, allowances and the expired collective agreement.

Under the reported agreement, the outstanding promotion processes for 51,000 teachers are expected to be completed by October 16, with the remaining cases to be addressed by the end of October.

The statement also cited plans for the modalities for the Deprived Area Allowance to be addressed in January 2027, the Digital Support Allowance in November and the Continuous Professional Development (CPD) Allowance in December.

The Council said it would monitor the implementation of the commitments and called on the FWSC, GES and teacher unions to work proactively to meet the agreed timelines.

It further urged school-based PTA executives to collaborate with school management to recover contact hours lost during the strike.

The Council said the reopening of schools would ease the burden on parents who had spent the period managing their children’s learning while continuing to meet their family responsibilities.

It also warned that prolonged school closures affect businesses and livelihoods linked to education, including school transport operators, uniform sellers, bookshops, food vendors and suppliers to the Ghana School Feeding Programme.

The NC-PTAs called on parents and guardians in public basic and secondary schools to ensure their wards were ready to resume classes on Monday.

“No Teacher, No School. No School, No Future,” the statement added.

Ghana News.title: Government procures over 2,000 transformers as Ghana’s electricity access hits 89.13% – Energy Minister
Ghana News.content:
Minister for Energy and Green Transition, Dr John Abdulai Jinapor

The Minister for Energy and Green Transition, Dr John Abdulai Jinapor, has announced that the government has procured more than 2,000 transformers to strengthen electricity distribution, improve power reliability and support growing demand across the country.

He said the investment formed part of broader interventions in generation, transmission and distribution aimed at improving the stability and efficiency of Ghana’s power system.

Addressing the 2026 Energy Sector Performance Review Retreat, Dr Jinapor disclosed that electricity access had increased to 89.13 per cent, while installed generation capacity had reached 5,854 megawatts (MW).

He added that renewable energy capacity had also increased to 345MW, reflecting progress in efforts to diversify the country’s energy mix.

The minister acknowledged that 2026 had been a particularly challenging year for the power sector, especially following the fire at the Akosombo Switchyard in April, which resulted in the loss of more than 1,000MW and placed considerable pressure on the national electricity system.

He commended the Volta River Authority (VRA) and the Ghana Grid Company Limited (GRIDCo) for their technical response and coordination during the incident.

“I commend VRA and GRIDCo for the technical expertise, resilience and coordination they demonstrated during that difficult period, and for their efforts to minimise the impact on the national system,” he said.

Dr Jinapor said the government had continued investing in transmission infrastructure, with several projects ongoing across the country. He cited the commencement of the process towards constructing the Ho–Asiekpe transmission line as part of efforts to strengthen the national grid.

“We were recently here to boost the transmission system and commence the process towards the construction of the Ho–Asiekpe transmission line. These investments are critical because generation alone is not enough,” he stated.

“We must have the transmission and distribution infrastructure to deliver reliable power to homes, businesses and industry,” he added.

On generation, the minister disclosed that eight of the ten units of the Anwomaso Thermal Plant had been commissioned, with six currently in service. He said the project was expected to generate 250MW by the end of 2026.

He further revealed that the renegotiation of independent power producer (IPP) agreements had received approval from Cabinet and Parliament, supporting the government’s efforts to improve the financial sustainability of the power sector.

Dr Jinapor also provided an update on the proposed Accra–Kumasi 330kV transmission line, indicating that the consultant tender had been evaluated and the scoping report and Environmental and Social Impact Assessment (ESIA) had been completed.

Despite the progress, he said outstanding challenges relating to transmission infrastructure, distribution efficiency, project financing and the implementation of key programmes required continued attention.

Looking towards 2027, the minister said the government would focus on translating plans and commitments into measurable outcomes, while expanding electricity access and ensuring that additional generation capacity was delivered in line with growing demand.

He also called for accelerated implementation of renewable energy initiatives, including solar projects, the completion of 35 mini-grids, expansion of solar home systems and net-metering, clean cooking initiatives and advancement of the Ghana Nuclear Power Programme.

“Let us therefore use the lessons of 2026 to strengthen our institutions, deepen our resilience, improve our performance and deliver tangible results for the Ghanaian people,” he said.

Dr Jinapor said the broader objective was to establish an energy sector that was reliable, affordable, sustainable and resilient enough to support Ghana’s economic transformation.

Ghana News.title: UTAG-UG threatens strike on October 19 over unpaid allowance
Ghana News.content:
University of Ghana

The University of Ghana branch of the University Teachers Association of Ghana (UTAG-UG) has threatened to withdraw teaching and related services from Monday, October 19, 2026, if the government fails to pay its members’ 2026 Book and Research Allowance.

In a notice of intention to embark on industrial action dated October 9, 2026, the association said the planned action was in response to persistent delays in the payment of the allowance.

The notice, addressed to the National Labour Commission, said the delay was contrary to a Memorandum of Agreement signed between UTAG and the government in 2020, which provides for the allowance to be paid by the end of August each year.

UTAG-UG has given the government until Friday, October 16, 2026, to settle the outstanding payments.

“Given the current circumstances, if by Friday 16th October 2026 these monies are not paid, members of UTAG-UG will withdraw all teaching and related services beginning Monday 19th of October 2026,” the notice stated.

The letter was signed by the association’s president, Dr. Jerry Joe Harrison, and its secretary, Godfred Bright Hagan.

Copies of the notice were sent to the Fair Wages and Salaries Commission, the ministers responsible for Employment and Labour Relations, Finance and Education, the Director of the Ghana Tertiary Education Commission, and the national president of UTAG.

The latest threat follows earlier warnings by the University of Ghana branch over delays in the payment of the allowance, which supports lecturers’ academic and research activities.

The proposed withdrawal of services could disrupt teaching and other related academic activities at the University of Ghana if the outstanding payments are not made before the deadline.

Ghana News.title: Let The Constitution direct Chieftaincy to deliver “All Development Is Local”
Ghana News.content:
By Kwasi Ansu-Kyeremeh, The Chieftaincy Institute

Chieftaincy’s natural power and capacity to lead local development have been grossly underrated and it is time to address that constitutionally. For accelerated local development, there is an urgent need to reverse the constitutional usurpation of that local development role which it assigns to local government.

Article 245(a) of Ghana’s 1992 Constitution mandates a decentralised system of local government and administration to drive local development. So far, the article has underperformed in implementation, such that the Constitution Review Committee (CRC) seeks its review in an “all development is local” approach.

To fix the local development deficit, CRC recommends “introduce direct elections for local government chief executives (MMDCEs),” instead of currently being appointed; together with the establishment of an Independent Devolution Commission (IDC) to intensify decentralisation and invigorate local development authority.

That sets a task for the Constitution Review Implementation Committee (CRIC) to enact constitutional intervention to remedy the little development at the local level which tends to slow national development. For that transformative local governance for accelerated local development, chieftaincy (as in occupiers of skins and stools), stands ready for consideration by CRIC as the logical apparatus. Even so, item 12 (electing MMDCEs) of the 13 points of action by CRIC seems far less capable of addressing that task of an article of local empowerment for local development as “fapem” (bedrock) of national development

Yet, dare one mention chieftaincy as the more viable agency for accelerated local development, and an initial reaction will likely be that it is too dividing and less uniting over succession issues to champion development. Fact, though, is that the negative of chieftaincy as source of conflict is overblown, while the institution’s massive potential as agent for local development, is woefully underrated.

A constitution is made to last, but it must first tackle the now issues. They say “72% of Ghanaian youth have considered leaving the country” for lack of employment opportunity. Tertiary students and graduates are actively involved in galamsey. The National Development Planning Commission (NDPC) attributes the syndrome of abandoned projects to “political discontinuity” and “lack of legal enforcement.” And despite legislation, public procurement abuse is widespread. As macro issues that they might be, they have implications for local development.

Historically, though, Biadanhene (chief) Nana Kwasi Ansu in the Berekum Traditional Area led his people to provide themselves with real development. Within two short years in the 1950s, the chiefdom provided itself with pipe-borne water and a community centre with day nursery annexed building complex. A farm trail was upgraded to a motorable road; and a generating plant was procured to supply electricity. Such micro activity can serve as the foundation for national development.

These days, from the village head (adikrofoɔ) through subchiefs (abrempɔn) to paramount chiefs (amanhene) all the way to the Asantehene, chiefs are still able to utilise their paltry traditionally decentralised authority to develop their areas. They mobilise to provide health and education facilities, social amenities and infrastructure to stimulate economic activity for the development of their chiefdoms. Just imagine what chieftaincy can do with its authority boosted by the constitution.

Basically, chieftaincy is “democratic government to a degree of which there is not any modern parallel in Europe,” with decentralisation as “one of its outstanding characteristics.” It is centripetally bottom-up and, therefore, naturally sensitive to local development. Chieftaincy democracy develops where “election democracy” may not. Thus, the institution deserves the restoration of its authority to develop which is constitutionally usurped in local government with the 1992 Constitution.

At each level of the chieftaincy hierarchy, the leader/chief is sufficiently empowered and reseanobly resourced with the autonomy and power to mobilise at each level of the hierarchy to develop the jurisdiction/chiefdom; no dependence on the centre to decentralise/devolve/disburse authority or resources before initiating, planning and implementing local development.

Traditional leaders are more knowledgeable, have richer lived life experiences and, by that, better prepared as development leaders than the political class. The former are empowered and compelled by culture, tradition and customary practice to mobilise human and material (land) resources to improve the living conditions of their people. And the institution’s gender inclusive queenmother role strengthens the active participation of women in the thinking and doing of local development that leads to national development.

Among the tools available to the chief for the mobilisation and execution of a local development agenda are the network of vertical sub-authorities in subchiefs, courtiers and other chiefly actors and the horizontal abusua (family/clan) groups with defined heads. A chief also has the power to create nkɔsoɔ (development) and boafoɔ (helper) stool occupants to specifically spearhead development activity. Also at his disposal are devices such as the dawuro concept for effective communication. Some skins and stools own communication centres, radio stations, websites or are robustly present on various social media platforms.

Alternatively, whatever its strengths, the imported local government, as is practised now by Chapter 20 of the 1992 Constitution, is severely limited productively, satisfactorily and effectively as a replacement for chieftaincy in promoting development at the grassroots. Decentralised authority for the local to develop itself within the broader national context is endlessly pursued or it “has collapsed;” or “dysfunctional.” Others think it is “centralisation of decentralistion;” that the central government develops the underdevelopment of the local area.

With its built-in politics of ampɛbrɛ (shuns hard work), ammɔbra (unachieved), kakistocratic and kleptocratic tendencies, local government political actors are engaged in some kind of operation hide the loot, employing all schemes to evade asset tracking and lifestyle audit accountability. Indeed, chieftaincy’s organic dynamics surpasses the superficial workings of local government in linking the people to their life struggles.

What is missing in a development transformative role for chieftaincy is the constitutional mandate to develop as assigned to local governemnent in Article 245(a)(b) of the 1992 Constitution. With chieftaincy, if there are lapses in development thought and action, it is possibly due to development being voluntary and not being required by law.

A constitutionally reorganised Chief-in-Council (CiC) local governance system that incorporates the tappable elements of both chieftaincy and local government. It inherits chieftaincy’s already effectively decentralised structure and quality leadership that thinks and does great local development. A lead chief (rotational among peers) would preside over a council of elected and appointed on merit membership. Term limits are to be enforced and where there is only one senior chief, the next (set) in grade shall be promoted to occupy the position (by rotation).

Structurally, the CiC has the features of: 1) merged authority 2) enhanced resourcing 3) guaranteed tenure and, therefore, continuity of programmes and projects post-election changes, 4) accountability and transparency 5) effective monitoring and supervision 6) quality leadership in a combination of knowledge and lived life experience, not ampɛbrɛ and ammɔbra political appointees and 7) prospects for rapid industrialisation.

It is proposed for the consideration of the CRIC, that the CiC organ will be the constitutional replacement for the current dualised paralleling local governance system of chieftaincy and local government. Its structure also incorporates advisory committees which might co-opt outside expertise to enhance decision-making and implementation. A specialised standing committee on women and associated issues, is to be chaired by the queenmother. Committees will deliberate the affairs of the units for in-depth knowledge to guide policy formulation and implementation.

An administrator, appointed on merit, will run a bureaucracy organised into functional units. Each unit is to be headed by a person with technical knowledge of the area. Among unit responsibilities are to research, offer technical advice and help implement programmes and projects.

One envisages enhanced opportunity of increased economic activity with the chief in charge to push for rapid industrialisation and development of the people in local communities. With a key focus on job creation, the chief-led CiC may want to explore clues and cues from Nkrumah’s cottage industries, Busia’s rural industries, Kufuor’s presidential initiatives and Akufo-Addo’s one village one dam/one district one factory as they affected local industrialisation.

CONCLUSION

It is time the Constitution took advantage of our own indigenous institutions to define and pursue our common development destiny by constitutionally redirecting the effort and resources for improving the local government system towards strengthening the empowerment of the chieftaincy institution to deliver “all development is local,” especially by strengthening its leadership accountability mechanisms. For a meaningful impact on the lives of ordinary Ghanaians, any change in the constitution regarding local development must necessarily begin with the recognition of chieftaincy as the primary local development agency. It is the people, with leadership of occupants of skins and stools who combine sukuu nyansa (knowledge) and efie nyansa (wisdom) with rich life experiences. That makes the traditional leader better prepared for executing the local development task than the transient political actors of less connection to the people and less so equipped to lead to develop.

Chieftaincy is unable to vigorously pursue its development responsibility because the authority to do so is usurped by the constitutional local government. Presently, lapses in development thought and action partly because the chief’s development responsibility not mandatory but rather voluntary. Chieftaincy must be treated as transformable, constitutionally formulated as transformative development apparatus for the aggressive pursuit of an “all development is local” agenda. That must be the focus and product of a CRIC organised 12th of the13 points of constitutional review.

Otherwise, the huge costs of the review of the 1992 Constitution since 2010 would have effectively betrayed the people and failed the CRC’s cardinal recommendation of local development for, and as, national development. Lest we forget the grassroots chant the authors/originators of the 1992 Constitution have forgotten by grabbing USD1.7 billion gold heist: “Ghana people we are always fighting for our rights. We no go sit down make dɛm cheat us every day. Daabi da!!!” Just imagine a constitution that mandates chiefs as the main agency for the development of their chiefdoms. It will no longer be “their” intervention project or programme but us empowered to develop of us, for us, in us, by us, about us, and to us!!!

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”

World.title: US lifts sanctions on daughter of military-linked Myanmar businessman
World.content:
Share US lifts sanctions on daughter of military-linked Myanmar businessman on social media

The United States has removed sanctions on the daughter of a Myanmar businessman accused of supporting the military-installed government.

The US Department of the Treasury removed Theint Win Htet from its sanctions list on Friday, according to its website, after she sued them in July.

The decision followed a Reuters news agency report that said US President Donald Trump’s administration has opened talks with Myanmar’s government, a break from years of US policy that sanctioned the generals responsible for a coup in 2021 against Myanmar’s democratically elected government.

In January 2024, the Treasury Department under former President Joe Biden’s administration targeted the Shwe Byain Phyu Group of Companies, which was founded by Theint Win Htet’s father, Thein Win Zaw, along with his family.

The department said the company supplied fuel to the military and owned at least 20 firms with close ties to the military leadership.

Theint Win Htet originally requested her removal in a lawsuit filed against the Biden administration. That case was dismissed last year. She then filed a second complaint in July, arguing that she has no role in her father’s business.

The sanctions had blocked her US credit cards, restricted her foreign bank accounts and forced her to abandon her master’s degree at Columbia University in New York. She now lives in Thailand with her mother, who was taken off the US sanctions list last year.

Theint Win Htet’s lawyer, Washington, DC-based sanctions specialist Erich Ferrari, filed a notice with the federal court in the US capital on Friday to voluntarily dismiss the lawsuit after her delisting.



‘Deplorable’

The group Justice For Myanmar has condemned the Treasury Department’s decision, saying Myanmar’s military is escalating attacks on civilians.

“It is deplorable that the US government continues to delist Myanmar cronies and their family members that provide funding for the junta’s terror,” the ‌group ‌said.

The Biden administration imposed sanctions on military officers and companies after the 2021 coup, which sparked a civil war that has killed about 100,000 people and displaced more than 3.5 million.

Washington lifted sanctions in July last year on several other Myanmar nationals and a company accused of aiding the military.

World.title: Ronaldo returns after Portugal quarrel to score in Al-Nassr win
World.content:
Cristiano Ronaldo opened the scoring for Al-Nassr in their 3-0 win over Diriyah, his first game since Portugal walkout.

Share Ronaldo returns after Portugal quarrel to score in Al-Nassr win on social media

Cristiano Ronaldo returned to club football action on Friday after a controversial international break with Portugal and scored the opening goal as Al-Nassr beat Diriyah 3-0 in the Saudi Pro League.

The victory put the defending champions level on points behind leader Al-Qadsiah on goal difference in the eighth round.

During the international window, the 41-year-old Ronaldo walked out of the Portugal squad, for which he has scored 146 goals in 234 appearances.

In a long statement posted on Tuesday, Ronaldo said Portugal coach Jorge Jesus had not been true to his word about when he would play the striker in the Nations League.

Ronaldo won the Saudi Arabia title in May with Jesus as Al-Nassr coach, and opened the scoring on Friday midway through the first half.

Kingsley Coman’s shot from outside the area was blocked by goalkeeper Waleed Abdullah, and Ronaldo was there to shoot home the rebound from close range for goal number 980 in his career.

Samu Costa added a second for Al-Nassr, coached by former Tottenham Hotspur boss Ange Postecoglou, just before the break, and Coman sealed the win with 13 minutes remaining.

Al-Qadsiah earlier thrashed Al-Kholood 5-0, with Dutch international Tijjani Reijnders opening the scoring and Italy’s Mateo Retegui and Mexico’s Julian Quinones also finding the target.
