World.title: ‘How can you stop these kids?’ Indian capital on lockdown before protests
World.content:
Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi has pulled out all the stops to prevent Cockroach movement protests taking over New Delhi.

Share ‘How can you stop these kids?’ Indian capital on lockdown before protests on social media

New Delhi, India – Heavy police barricades line the streets around Connaught Place, the colonial-era square near Jantar Mantar, on Saturday morning as police have begun detaining groups of protesters arriving for planned demonstrations.

They are here in support of the influential Gen-Z movement and Cockroach Janta Party, which have called for the resignation of India’s election chief, amid a bitter dispute over who gets to vote in the world’s most populous democracy.

Protesters are demanding sweeping reforms and a rollback of a controversial voter revision exercise which has struck 130 million names from the voter list.

For now, an eerie silence hangs over parts of central New Delhi. Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s government has gone to lengths to turn the city into a fortress, deploying nearly 30,000 personnel onto the streets.

Police ⁠have also detained the founder of ⁠the Cockroach Janta Party, Abhijeet Dipke.

Indian TV channels reported early on Saturday that officers met Dipke at New Delhi airport ⁠after he arrived ⁠from the financial capital Mumbai and asked him to call ⁠off the protest as authorities ⁠had banned it.

CJP leaders ⁠Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka were also detained from their flight ‌upon landing, the movement said in a statement.

On Friday, the government extraordinarily cancelled all trains to New Delhi; locked down more than 50 metro stations; imposed an internet shutdown; and sent personnel to thousands of students in local communities to warn them against participation in the protest.



Several students en route to New Delhi from different states of India were dragged out of trains and buses and detained by the police. Many have been placed under house arrest in cities hundreds of kilometres away from New Delhi.

The Cockroach movement says thousands have been detained across India as Modi’s government intensifies its crackdown. Yet undeterred protesters have pledged to keep returning to the streets.

‘Made EMERGENCY official’

Current restrictions in the Indian capital and the nationwide crackdown on protesters have evoked memories of the 1975 Emergency, when then-Prime Minister Indira Gandhi suspended civil liberties, censored the press and jailed political opponents.

“Narendra Modi just made EMERGENCY official,” Dipke, the founder of the Cockroach movement, wrote in a post on X. “This intimidation is not going to work, Modi. The youth of this country are no longer scared of you.”

Neha Bora, the firebrand Gen-Z protest leader and the national president of the left student body All India Students’ Association, equated the Modi government with British colonialist forces that unsuccessfully clamped down on India’s independence movement. She called on the masses to join the protest.

On Saturday morning, young people were trying to respond to her call despite the police restrictions in place.

Santosh Kumar, 29, a street sweeper in the outer circle of Connaught Place, told Al Jazeera he feels frustrated seeing teenagers detained at police barricades.

“How can you stop these kids? They are detaining 10; 50 more are coming. Modi, the dictator’s time is up: He will not even stay until 2029 (the time of the next elections).

“This is the time we turn Delhi into Nepal and Bangladesh – learn from them and take back our country,” he said, referring to youth-led movements in those countries.

Sameer Irshad, 28, an engineer from Gurugram, approached the barricades near Connaught Place while pushing his 57-year-old mother Sheeba Abdi in a wheelchair.

Abdi told us: “This sort of crackdown, where we cannot peacefully express our dissent, is unseen in Delhi. Why has government turned this place into a fortress? Why are they so scared of citizens like me?”

Under house arrest

Last month, India was shaken by revelations of divisions within the supposedly autonomous body that is in charge of conducting elections, over controversial policies that critics say have disenfranchised tens of millions of people.



India’s Election Commission chief, Gyanesh Kumar, was accused of overruling concerns raised by the two other election commissioners about the integrity of ongoing changes in the voter database, an investigation by The Indian Express reported.

India is among the few countries to have taken an active approach to enrolling every last voter.

Critics say the ongoing revision of the voter list flips the foundational principle of Indian democracy: Demanding that citizens prove their voting rights, and disproportionately targeting Muslims, economically weaker sections, minorities and other vulnerable groups in Indian society.

Arif, a 24-year-old district coordinator for the Students’ Federation of India, another left-wing student organisation to have joined the protest call, was locked in his home in Saharanpur, nearly 200km (125 miles) from New Delhi, on Thursday.

“Several police officials started beating my door out of nowhere late at night, asking my parents for details of my whereabouts,” Arif, who did not want to give his full name, told Al Jazeera from his home in Saharanpur, where he is currently detained under the police’s watch around the clock.

“They just want to stop me from going to Delhi for protest. They are threatening to book me under criminal cases and destroy my future,” he said, adding that this is the first time he has been subject to such detention.

“I really wanted to be in Delhi, to fight and reclaim our democracy. The time for Modi is over,” he said.

Modi ‘at his weakest’

This week, Modi and his Bharatiya Janata Party (BNP) celebrated his 25 years in office, starting with his years as chief minister of the western state of Gujarat – where he oversaw the infamous 2002 Muslim pogrom – and later as India’s prime minister since 2014.

But Modi has never looked weaker in power than now, analysts and Indian political observers argue.

In July, the Cockroach-led protests choked key New Delhi streets and forced out Modi’s education minister, Dharmendra Pradhan.

This time, Modi has taken more extreme measures to prevent protesters from gaining a foothold in central New Delhi, “because he wishes to retain the aura and image of a leader who never yields to public pressure, someone who is invincible”, said Nilanjan Mukhopadhyay, an author and biographer of Modi.

“Modi appears at the lowest point [of his political life] in public perception. This is extremely paradoxical because he has some of the most important autonomous institutions, large sections of the bureaucracy, and state wings in tight control and acting at his behest,” Mukhopadhyay told Al Jazeera.

In the face of growing protests, Modi is now “fast losing people’s perception of being a leader who leads them out of livelihood pits”, he said.

Prashant Bhushan, a senior lawyer at the Supreme Court and a rights activist who planned to join the protest on Saturday, told Al Jazeera that “Modi’s government looks quite scared of the people.

“People in India are rising and demanding answers. And when the government gets scared, they adopt draconian measures to stay in power,” Bhushan said. “But only more and more people will rise from repression.”

World.title: Yemen’s Taiz under siege again as food and fuel prices rise
World.content:
Houthi advances and the closure of vital roads into Taiz have triggered shortages, reviving memories of earlier siege.

Share Yemen’s Taiz under siege again as food and fuel prices rise on social media

Taiz, Yemen – Taiz is under siege, but 37-year-old Iskandar Abdullah already knows what it’s like to live under one.

The city, a major population centre in Yemen’s southwest, endured a devastating Houthi siege between 2015 and 2016, as the Iranian-backed group attempted to capture the city from local pro-government forces. The Houthis continued to maintain a partial siege in the following years through their control over other access points into the city.

“They were difficult days,” Abdullah recalls, even as the Houthis begin a new siege on Taiz following their capture of territory to the south of the city, cutting off the main road to government-held territory. “We witnessed the horrors of the siege and experienced the bitterness of life in all its terrifying details.”

“I hope those painful days never return.”

In early September, the Houthis launched an offensive along the Red Sea coast of Taiz governorate. The group soon established full control over the port city of Mocha and the district of Dhubab, where the Bab al-Mandeb strait – through which 12 percent of global trade passes – is located.

The Houthis, who have controlled Yemen’s populous northwest, including the capital Sanaa, since the country’s war started in 2014, did not stop their military attacks at the Red Sea. Even as government forces, backed by Saudi Arabia, began a counteroffensive in early October and regained some of the territory lost, the Houthis pressed forward in the countryside surrounding Taiz.

The Houthis successfully captured the town of al-Turbah by October 4, severing the only remaining main road between Taiz city and other government-held areas.



Taiz residents, like Abdullah, are now worried that the city is about to face a prolonged full-scale siege. Abdullah remembers how difficult life was between 2015 and 2016, when pro-government forces were confined to an enclave in the centre of the city.

Locals endured “horrors, as well as appalling humanitarian and economic conditions unlike anything experienced by any other Yemeni governorate during the war”, according to Abdullah.

“People lacked even the most basic necessities of life, including drinking water, food, fuel and medicine,” he said. “The only exceptions were supplies smuggled across rugged mountain terrain, carried on the backs of people and donkeys, including oxygen cylinders for the sick and wounded.”

Shortages

The siege was eventually broken in 2016 when pro-government forces recaptured territory south of Taiz city. In 2024, under domestic and international pressure, the Houthis agreed to reopen another important route into the city from the east, connecting it to Sanaa and other Houthi-controlled areas of northern Yemen.

However, with the recent resumption of fighting, the vital crossing has been closed following attempted incursions by Houthi fighters, according to security sources who spoke to Al Jazeera.

The closure has severed a crucial route that had become essential for Taiz residents – much of the city’s food supplies had entered through the crossing.

Nabil Jamil, director-general of the planning and development office in Taiz governorate, said that the current siege on Taiz is “more comprehensive and its impact more severe than in 2015”.

“This time, the siege does not only affect the governorate’s main roads, but also most of the secondary roads connecting the rural districts themselves,” Jamil said.

Jamil said that approximately 2.8 million people had been living in government-held areas of Taiz governorate, alongside another 200,000 people who have been recently displaced by the fighting along the coast and rural Taiz.

“All of them will face humanitarian hardship and deteriorating living conditions as a result of the siege,” he said.

Less than a week into the renewed siege, the city’s streets appeared almost deserted because of a fuel shortage, which had previously entered the city through the al-Turbah route from Aden.

On the black market, the price of a 20-litre (5.2-gallon) container of petrol rose from 30,000 Yemeni riyals ($19) to 90,000 Yemeni riyals ($58).



Meanwhile, markets and grocery shops have seen a surge in demand, as residents rush to stock up on food amid fears that supplies would disappear from shelves because of the siege.

Some residents have accused traders of hoarding and monopolising essential goods in the absence of any effective market oversight.

“Food markets in Taiz have witnessed a noticeable increase in the prices of basic commodities, particularly wheat and flour, while the prices of vegetables and fruits have doubled, as the siege has made it difficult to bring these products into the city,” said Wafiq Saleh, a journalist specialising in economic affairs.

“Traders in the city have food stocks sufficient to last several months,” he added. “Nevertheless, some traders began raising prices as soon as the fighting intensified on the outskirts of the city.”

Humanitarian fears

Fighting is continuing in the Taiz countryside, and there is hope among locals that government forces will be able to retake the areas lost to the Houthis in recent days, or continue their forward momentum in areas to the west of Taiz city, and break the siege from that direction.

But for now, the Houthis appear to be on the front foot in the areas to Taiz city’s south.

Salman al-Maqrami, a journalist specialising in Houthi affairs, believes the primary objective of the Taiz siege is to undermine the cohesion of the forces opposed to them in the city, which has long been a hotbed of hostility towards the group.

“Therefore, there is no doubt that [the Houthis] are seeking revenge against this population that opposes them,” he added.

The fall of Taiz would also be symbolic for the Houthis, allowing the group to present itself as being able to threaten any area under government control, even if the population is hostile.

However, Nabil Sharyan, a lawyer and the head of the Justice for Rights and Development Organization (JRDO), pointed out that the effect of any such battle for Taiz – including a longstanding siege on such a large city – would be detrimental to civilians.

“Civilians must never be turned into a means of exerting pressure in any conflict,” Sharyan said.

He warned of the enormous humanitarian cost of the renewed siege, “particularly for patients, children, women and the elderly, given the difficulties in accessing hospitals, medical services, and medicines”.

“Restrictions on travel and movement will also affect students, patients, employees and families who depend on travelling between different areas of the governorate and beyond,” he added.

Sharyan called on the international community, human rights organisations and humanitarian agencies to take a clear position that “guarantees residents access to their basic needs, ensures that roads and crossings remain open to civilians and goods, and allows patients to reach healthcare services, in a manner that safeguards human dignity and fundamental rights”.



Jamil said that local authorities in Taiz had sent a letter to the United Nations seeking assistance in addressing the crisis and its humanitarian consequences.

Local authorities’ priorities include opening safe roads and corridors for civilians, especially those who need to travel for medical treatment, and allowing medicine and food to reach Taiz.

“We are still waiting for a response or intervention on the ground,” Jamil said.

World.title: Trump announces deal for Russian diesel as Zelensky calls it a gift to Putin
World.content:
Ukraine's President Volodymr Zelensky has condemned Donald Trump's announcement of a deal to import Russian diesel into the US.

Zelensky called it a gift to Russian President Vladimir Putin that amounts to "an investment in a war that must be ended, not prolonged".

Trump said Putin had agreed to release 300,000 tonnes of diesel immediately "to the American and global marketplace" followed by 500,000 tonnes in November and another million after that.

It is understood the US Treasury is suspending sanctions on Russian diesel exports until 7 April as part of the deal, but other assets like those in American banks are still frozen.

In his Truth Social post, Trump added that a further three million tonnes of Russian diesel would be delivered "within a short period", dependent on the condition of its refineries, which have been attacked by Ukraine.

Putin later said Russia, which introduced a ban on diesel exports earlier this year, was willing to supply both the US and global markets with oil and petroleum products, but his statement did not specify amounts.

In a post on social media, Zelensky said Russia would repay the diesel with "further terror".

"We count on America's fair support for our defence of life, for our defence of people in Ukraine â and on the United States having a correspondingly strong conversation with Russia. A strong one, not a weak one," he wrote.

Analysts, however, have questioned whether Russia is capable of providing that quantity of diesel and the extent to which doing so will ease prices for American consumers.

World.title: Analysis: Trump's shock Russia deal highlights mounting pressure to curb fuel prices
World.content:
For months, the American president has been searching for ways to ease his party's political pain.

He recently pressured European allies to further tap their oil reserves. He deferred federal taxes on the fuel and authorised supplies designated for farm use to be used in interstate trucking.

He has also promised that he would not renew attacks on Iran until after the midterms â an unusually frank acknowledgement of the political impact the ongoing conflict is having.

His decision to strike a deal with Russia's Putin is only the latest, most dramatic effort.

Trump's Truth Social posts often provide incomplete information, of course. The details of exactly how Russia is supplying this fuel to the global market, and what they might get for in return â besides much-needed hard currency â is unclear.

It opens Trump to criticism from European allies and American politicians that his administration is now helping to fund the Russian war machine.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky called the deal a "gift" to Putin that Russia would "repay" with "terror and perfidy".

"Allowing Russia to sell petroleum products is an investment in a war that must be ended, not prolonged," he wrote on X.

It is also uncertain exactly how much Trump's move will help Republicans at the ballot box.

The promised European diesel release hasn't moved energy prices significantly, and there's no information on the speed with which Russian fuel could enter the market.

Its diesel refinery capacity has been damaged by repeated Ukrainian strikes â attacks that Trump has encouraged Zelensky to curtail.

The US uses approximately 3.6 million barrels of diesel a day, so even if Russia delivers its promised 300,000 tons this month, that amounts to approximately half of the US daily consumption.

Americans may not notice much of an immediate difference.

With less than a month before November's midterm elections, early voting has already started in many states. The political cake, as the saying goes, is all but baked.

"Lower prices for Americans, especially our Great Farmers, Ranchers, and Truckers, is my Greatest Priority," Trump wrote in his Truth Social post.

But over the past seven months, prices on energy, fuel and consumer goods have only gone up - even as Trump and his officials have repeatedly assured an uneasy public a successful resolution to the war, and an easing of its economic impact, is nearly at hand.

Trump may be left hoping that his latest deal, setting aside its potentially uncomfortable diplomatic issues, will be enough to convince American voters that his promise of impending economic relief is more than just empty words.

World.title: Three men found guilty of murdering Australian brothers and US friend in Mexico
World.content:
Three men have been found guilty of murdering Australian brothers Jake and Callum Robinson, and their US friend Carter Rhoad during a surfing trip in Mexico in 2024.

The men's full names could not be given for legal reasons, and they were only identified as JesÃºs Gerardo, Irineo Francisco and Ãngel JesÃºs. They are yet to be sentenced - but are likely to spend the rest of their lives in a prison.

Debra Robinson, the brothers' mother, told the courtroom that her sons' murders had taken "the future we had imagined with them".

During the trial in the northern Baja California state, the court heard that the tourists were killed in an apparent botched robbery of their truck in a secluded beach area.

Their bodies were later found dumped down a well with gunshot wounds to their heads.

The murders sent shockwaves around the world, particularly in Australia, as the coastal area is usually safe from the violence seen in other parts of Mexico.

Debra Robinson and her husband Martin have been at the court in the coastal town of Ensenada throughout the trial, and delivered emotional testimony during closing arguments before Friday's verdict.

"It's hard for a parent to lose a son, and we lost two sons," Martin said.

Family members of Carter Rhoad joined the trial by video link.

Speaking to media outside court a week ago, Debra Robinson said the couple were "deeply grateful" to Australians for the outpouring of support they had received and that they "feel the love and their arms around us".

During the month-long trial, the prosecution had sought 150 years in prison for each of the three defendants.

In November last year, the girlfriend of the alleged ringleader, JesÃºs Gerardo alias "El Kekas", was sentenced in a separate trial to 20 years in prison. She had admitted to involvement in the robbery.

At the time, the murders shocked locals and tourists in Ensenada who were disturbed at the apparent ease and sheer pointlessness of the killings.

The beach town has a reputation as a welcoming spot for surfers, but the chilling murders revealed how commonplace such extreme violence remains in Mexico.

The only explanation the authorities were able to give was that the surfers - all in their early 30s - had ultimately been murdered for being in the wrong place at the wrong time.

Their killings happened barely 36 hours after they crossed into Mexico from the US. Their bodies, however, were not found for another week when their families were able to identify them.

At the time, the surfer community in Ensenada turned out in force to honour the men by paddling out at a popular surfing spot and throwing flowers into the sea.

Local surfers also called for greater security for residents and visiting tourists, citing other recent examples of violence in the state. Tourism is a key part of the regional economy in Baja California.

Amid the demands for action, state Governor Marina del Pilar Ãvila tried to ease public fears about the widespread violence.

"Baja California is and will continue to be a state with safe tourism for the thousands of people who visit us from the rest of the country and the world", she said.

"I send my condolences and solidarity to the families at this difficult time."

World.title: Flydubai attacker began a 'drift towards extremism and terrorism' in Australia, UAE says
World.content:
According to Shamsi, interrogations of the 29-year-old pilot revealed he had been inspired by al-Qaeda's 11 September attacks in the US in 2001.

"The findings indicated that signs of his drift towards extremism and terrorism first emerged in 2017, while he was studying in Australia," the attorney-general was quoted as saying by the UAE's state news agency Wam on Friday.

"During that period, he was influenced by takfiri [radical] ideology through reading extremist literature and following online content glorifying terrorist organisations and suicide attacks."

The Wam report also said the pilot had told investigators "he had prepared himself both psychologically and physically to carry out the plot by intensifying his exposure to material promoting terrorism and training in boxing under a private coach".

"He admitted that he had acted alone, without the involvement of others, although investigations are continuing to verify this claim," Wam said.

The Australian Broadcasting Corporation has reported the man was issued an Australian student visa in 2014 and studied in the country in 2015-17, before leaving.

This week, the Sydney Morning Herald unearthed tweets from al-Mammami's now-deleted X account in which he referred to his five years spent studying abroad in Australia, Britain, and New Zealand, as "the golden years of my religious commitment".

More than 170 passengers and crew were on board flight FZ1073 on 30 September.

In the days after the incident, Australian authorities confirmed they were looking into the man's links to Australia.

The Victorian Joint Counter Terrorism Team - made up of the Australian Federal Police (AFP), Victoria Police and the country's security agency ASIO - said it was "investigating the man's links to Australia".

World.title: Hurricane Isaias downgraded after making landfall in Florida
World.content:
Hurricane Isaias, the first of the 2026 Atlantic season, made landfall Friday night along the northern Gulf Coast of Florida, bringing with it heavy rains, powerful winds and the risk of life-threatening flash flooding and storm surges.

Isaias is continuing north across the Southeastern United States after being downgrade from a hurricane to a post-tropical cyclone, the BBC's US partner CBS News reports, external.

Florida, Alabama, and Georgia have each issued states of emergency amid warnings of life-threatening storm surge that could cause up to 9 feet (2.7m) of flooding in some areas.

Isaias is one of three storm systems affecting North America this weekend, with the two others hitting Mexico and Southern California in the El-NiÃ±o fuelled warm waters of the Pacific Ocean.

Both Florida and Alabama instituted mandatory evacuations to thousands of people due to the storm.

In Florida, those evacuations include coastal communities in direct aim of the powerful storm. Florida Senator Rick Scott encouraged residents in designated areas to evacuate as soon as possible, as he warned in a social media post: "DO NOT WAIT! Get out NOW!"

Governor of Alabama Kay Ivey issued a mandatory evacuation for all non-residents, tourists and visitors in key counties likely to be heavily affected by the storm.

Hurricane Isaias is the first hurricane in the Atlantic's hurricane season, which largely has been delayed due to El NiÃ±o conditions in the Pacific.

It marks the first time in more than 30 years that a hurricane did not form till October.

The storm is likely to bring "life-threatening storm surge" to the US Gulf Coast, the National Hurricane Center (NHC) warned.

After hitting Florida, the centre of Isaias is forecast to move across Alabama and into the Tennessee Valley on Saturday and Sunday, the National Weather Service said late on Friday.

As of Friday evening, hurricane-force winds extended outward up to 35 miles (55 km) from Isaias' centre, and tropical storm-force winds extended as far as 205 miles (335 km).

On Saturday morning, the NHC said all hurricane warnings had been discontinued, while a storm surge warning is in effect for parts of Florida. There is also a tropical storm warning in the state, as well as in east Alabama.

World.title: US country music star Ella Langley cancels show due to 'security threat'
World.content:
US country music star Ella Langley has said she had to cancel her sold-out concert in Tulsa, Oklahoma on Friday night, due to a "serious security threat".

The singer made what she called the "incredibly difficult" decision around two hours before the show at the 19,000-seater arena was due to start.

In a post on Instagram, the 27-year-old said the threat involved "the safety of my fans, the venue staff and my team".

Cpt Richard Meulenberg from Tulsa Police Department said a person had called saying "great harm" would be done at the event with "shots fired and bombs."

He stated his team had checked the venue at BOK Center several times before the show and "could not find any threat".

"The event was ready to go," he added, saying officers with sniffer dogs did a sweep of the arena again after the phone call was made.

"We could not find a credible threat," he said, stressing that the person who had made the call "disrupted this entire event" for thousands of Langley fans.

The star - who did not give any further details - also apologised to her fans, saying additional information regarding ticket refunds "will be shared as soon as possible".

BOK Center issued its own statement, saying that "the safety and well-being of everyone involved is our absolute priority, and after careful consideration, we have determined that the show cannot proceed.

"We understand the disappointment this news brings and apologise to fans who planned to attend."

In September, Langley's country smash Choosin' Texas overtook Mariah Carey's All I Want for Christmas Is You to become the longest-running number one single in US chart history.

Its success helped the singer from Alabama to sweep the Academy of Country Music Awards in May.

World.title: Powerful magnitude 7.7 earthquake hits Panama, damaging buildings
World.content:
Verified footage shows one side of a cathedral in PenonomÃ© collapsed due to the shaking, as well as one of its spires.

Another video showed a local hotel had almost completely collapsed.

Ricardo Brown, who lives in the southern Herrera province, told news agency Reuters that the earthquake had damaged several homes in his neighbourhood of Las Minas.

"We're scared. It's just the two of us old folks here. The house has cracked and we're afraid it could fall on us," the 74-year-old said.

The full extent of the damage it has caused is not yet clear, though several large aftershocks were also reported near the initial earthquake, potentially complicating the situation on the surface.

The quake was registered as occurring at a depth of just 12km. The shallower the earthquake, the more likely it is to have more severe effects on the surface.

Many people were evacuated from buildings in Panama City, about 200km from the epicentre, and were seen taking to the streets or sitting in nearby parks until the shaking had ceased.

Damage in the capital appears to be limited to that caused by debris falling from roofs.

Panama's President JosÃ© RaÃºl Mulino said his entire government was mobilising in response to the earthquake, adding: "What happened should not be used to cause alarm or disorder."

World.title: 'Stain on the country': Trump criticises Norway over Nobel Peace Prize
World.content:
US President Donald Trump has once again made complaints that he did not receive the Nobel Peace Prize, calling this year's decision "disgraceful and embarrassing".

The prize was awarded to former International Criminal Court judge Navi Pillay on Friday. Hours after the announcement, Donald Trump told a rally he had "never heard" of the "mystery person".

"This is an indelible stain on the country of Norway" he said, adding "we will not forget".

Trump has been outspoken about his desire to win the prize, and made similar criticisms in 2025 when it was awarded to Venezuelan opposition leader MarÃ­a Corina Machado.

Last year, Norway's Prime Minister Jonas Gahr StÃ¸re explained to Trump it was an independent committee based in Norway, not the Norwegian government, which decides who will receive the prize.

Speaking to his supporters at a rally in Syracuse, New York, the US president repeated claims that he had settled eight wars and was "about to settle or win two more", without providing evidence.

"The Nobel Peace Prize has been forever discredited by a handful of radical ideologues who are anti-democracy and really enemies of civilisation," he said.

World.title: Nigeria’s Bangkok roadshow: Selling opportunity, pricing risk, By Adeola Akinremi
World.content:
In July 2007, I attended the second session of the Conference of the Parties to the Framework Convention on Tobacco Control in Thailand. It was my first real encounter with Bangkok, and I remember the city for its contradictions: the squalor and the splendour, the disorder and the beauty, the old pressed against the new. It was a city I could not easily forget.

Nearly two decades later, Bangkok is back in my mind for a very different reason.

Next week, Nigeria’s economic czars will travel to Bangkok. Dr. Taiwo Oyedele, the Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, will board an aircraft, carrying with him a pipe of promise, packaged in a polished presentation. Dr. Jumoke Oduwole, the Minister of Industry, Trade and Investment, will join him, making the case to investors at the 2026 World Bank/International Monetary Fund Annual Meetings that Nigeria remains a country of immense possibility. They will pitch Nigeria as a place where capital can come, grow and make money.

To demonstrate its determination, the Federal Ministry of Finance has put up a colourful, animated landing page on its website, complete with a countdown clock, outlining its plans and priorities for the Bangkok mission. The government says it will present 23 transactions with a total capital requirement of $42.7 billion across transport, energy and gas, agriculture, industry, housing and urban services at the meetings.

There is nothing unusual about a government courting investors. In fact, there is evidence that Nigeria is attracting capital. The IMF says Nigeria’s financial account recorded a net inflow of about $5.9 billion in 2025, mainly from portfolio investment. Net foreign direct investment improved to about $2.8 billion, still less than one per cent of GDP.

The IMF has also pointed to the importance of a credible macroeconomic and foreign-exchange framework, predictable regulation, reliable infrastructure and security in creating conditions for stronger foreign direct investment. These are not issues that a polished presentation can resolve. They require evidence of progress that investors can see, assess and trust.

Yes, Nigeria can attract money without attracting enough long-term investors. Portfolio capital can move relatively quickly when yields, exchange rates and market conditions change. But a factory, railway, power plant, logistics network or industrial facility cannot be moved so easily. These are precisely the kinds of investments Nigeria says it wants to attract in Bangkok.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

But there is an oddness to these journeys that is difficult to ignore. Nigeria is forever travelling in search of capital. London. New York. Washington. France. Now Bangkok.

We do not yet know how much investment will come from President Bola Tinubu’s recent meetings with investors in France. That uncertainty matters, especially at a time when investors are weighing Nigeria’s opportunities against the risks that shadow their decisions.

And that raises a question Nigeria should be asking itself before another delegation boards another aircraft. If the opportunity is as compelling as we say it is, why does Nigeria so often have to go abroad to make the case?

This question is more revealing than any roadshow presentation. It forces the government to consider what is on investors’ minds, rather than simply what Nigeria wants to offer them.

Nigeria does not need another sales pitch. It needs to convince investors that the risks of doing business in the country can be identified, understood and, most importantly, reduced.

Those risks operate at three levels: the country, the project and the cost of making it function.

At the country level, the investor wants to know: Can I get my money out? Can I rely on the rules? Can I enforce my rights? Are the courts swift, or does justice drift?

At the project level, the questions are: Can I price the risk? Can the project generate predictable cash flows?

Can the infrastructure support it?

These questions determine whether an opportunity is worth the investment. The problem is that investors are pricing both Nigeria and the projects on offer. A brilliant railway project can still be unattractive if investors believe the surrounding regulatory, currency, political or payment risks will overwhelm its economics. A project’s promise cannot be separated from the environment in which it must operate.

Then there is the cost of making the investment function. Consider a hypothetical investor interested in building a world-class cancer hospital in Nigeria. The investment could serve Nigerians and, by extension, patients from other African countries. But the investor does not simply calculate the cost of buying land, constructing the hospital and installing medical equipment. The investor must calculate the cost of making the hospital function.

What will it cost to secure a reliable electricity supply? How predictable is the process of importing specialised medical equipment through Apapa Wharf? Will port clearance and other procedures work efficiently, or will delays increase costs? Can the hospital depend on reliable internet connectivity? What additional expenses will be required to protect its staff, patients and equipment?

Every private workaround for unreliable infrastructure, inefficient processes or inadequate security adds to the cost of doing business.

This is why Nigeria’s infrastructure problem is not merely a development problem. It is an investment-pricing problem.

That is what Oyedele and Oduwole should prioritise. The more urgent task is to make those transactions investable through better preparation, credible guarantees, predictable regulation, appropriate local-currency financing, stronger project sponsors, transparent procurement and mechanisms that make risk measurable and, where possible, transferable.

A roadshow can introduce projects to investors and generate interest. It cannot, by itself, fix the conditions that determine whether those investors commit their money. That requires coordinated action across government, credible institutions and a willingness to address the practical constraints that make doing business in Nigeria expensive and uncertain.

At the end of the day, Nigeria does not need to become better at telling investors that the country is an opportunity. It needs to become better at making that opportunity impossible to ignore.

Adeola Akinremi is a public policy advisor, strategic communications expert, and the founder and CEO of Hintells, an AI-powered intelligence platform serving businesses and diplomatic missions in Washington, DC. He has extensive multilateral experience advising on governance, economic and policy reforms across global markets and can be reached at: [email protected]

World.title: Galatasaray explain Osimhen’s limited role after injury comeback
World.content:
Galatasaray assistant coach İrfan Saraloğlu has explained why Victor Osimhen was handed limited minutes on his return from injury, after the Nigerian striker provided an assist in the club’s 3-1 victory over Kasimpasa on Friday night.

Osimhen returned to action at Rams Park after recovering from the injury he sustained during Galatasaray’s 3-2 victory over Istanbul Başakşehir in September.

The Super Eagles forward came off the bench in the closing stages, replacing Deniz Gul with 13 minutes remaining as the Turkish champions looked to secure all three points.

Despite his limited time on the pitch, Osimhen made an immediate impact, setting up Gabonese midfielder Mario Lemina for Galatasaray’s decisive third goal in the closing minutes.

However, Saraloğlu revealed that the team’s approach changed after Lucas Torreira was sent off shortly after the hour mark, forcing Galatasaray to retreat and adjust their defensive shape.

“Our game in the second half, after the card, we retreated a bit, our balance was disrupted, but I can say that Sanchez was out of the game when the goal came. They scored from that gap,” he told Galatasaray’s official website.

The assistant coach also explained that Osimhen’s late introduction was a deliberate decision, with the club keen to manage his workload after his spell on the sidelines and avoid risking another setback.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“Osimhen just came back from injury, we had to protect him. We had to protect the players returning from national team duty too,” Saraloğlu added.

Osimhen will be encouraged by his productive return, having contributed directly to a goal despite playing only the final 13 minutes of the encounter.

The former Napoli striker had made an impressive start to the 2026/27 campaign before his injury, scoring six goals and providing two assists across four matches against Corum FK, Erzurumspor FK, Göztepe and Istanbul Başakşehir.

With his fitness gradually being managed, Osimhen will now look to regain full match sharpness and build on his early-season form as Galatasaray continue their campaign.

World.title: Three arrested over woman’s dead body found in Plateau
World.content:
Three suspects have been arrested after a woman’s dead body was discovered in Pankshin Local Government Area of Plateau State, the council chairman, Felix Gonung, has said.

The suspects have been transferred to the police headquarters in Jos after investigators reportedly recovered substances suspected to be fetish materials from them, Mr Gonung said.

The arrests come amid growing concerns over two bodies discovered in Pankshin within a month, with vital organs allegedly missing from the victims.

Speaking with journalists in Pankshin on Friday, Mr Gonung said the three suspects were arrested following the discovery of the woman’s body last month.

He also disclosed that security agencies were investigating the discovery of a young man’s body at Monday Market on 6 October.

The circumstances surrounding the two deaths remain unclear, and it has not been established whether the cases are connected.

Mr Gonung said the young man’s death might be linked to cult activities among students or criminal elements operating within the student community. He did not, however, provide evidence establishing such a link.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The chairman vowed to work with security agencies to address the incidents and prevent further loss of lives.

“I swore an oath to protect the lives and property of my people. However, the government’s security plans are confidential and the public will soon feel their results and impact,” he said.

“This administration, in collaboration with security agencies, is doing everything within its power to restore and maintain the long-existing peace in our communities.”

As part of the proposed security response, Mr Gonung said the council planned to introduce a policy requiring landlords and hotel operators to provide information about their tenants and guests.

He said the measure was intended to help identify criminal elements who might use rented accommodation or hotels as cover to perpetrate crimes.

“This will enable us to crack down on criminal syndicates who disguise themselves as students or guests to perpetrate crimes in the community,” he said.

Mr Gonung noted that Pankshin had enjoyed relative peace despite security challenges in other parts of Plateau State, adding that the recent incidents had heightened residents’ concerns.

He urged residents to remain vigilant and report suspicious activities to the appropriate authorities.

World.title: Bail Application: Court of Appeal rules against El-Rufai
World.content:
The Court of Appeal in Kaduna on Friday upheld the state high court’s decision that denied former Kaduna State Governor Nasir El-Rufai bail.

The Court of Appeal dismissed an appeal filed by Mr El-Rufai, challenging the decision of the Kaduna State High Court to deny him bail.

Delivering its judgment in Appeal Number CA/K/254C/2026, the Appellate Court affirmed the ruling of the lower court, holding that the trial judge exercised his discretion judicially and judiciously, with no miscarriage of justice.

In a unanimous decision, the three-member appellate panel held that Mr El-Rufai failed to establish fresh facts or special circumstances warranting interference with the lower court’s decision to deny him bail.

According to Channel Television, the lead judgement delivered by Justice Onyekachi Aja-Otisi affirmed the ruling of the lower court, which refused the former governor’s second bail application on 10 June.

The court also struck out the appellant’s reply brief filed on 29 September, describing it as incompetent, while resolving the sole issue for determination against Mr El-Rufai and in favour of the Federal Republic of Nigeria.

The appellate court held that it would not interfere with a trial court’s findings of fact where they were not shown to be perverse, and it dismissed the appeal for lack of merit.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The substantive trial has been scheduled to commence on 12 October, 2026.

The development comes days after Justice Darious Khobo of the Kaduna State High Court rejected Mr El-Rufai’s bail and recusal applications.

Mr El-Rufai’s ongoing prosecution by the Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission (ICPC) stems primarily from recommendations in a 2024 Kaduna State House of Assembly probe report that accused his 2015–2023 administration of mismanaging public funds.

The ICPC filed multiple charges against the former governor in federal and state courts, including one alleging that he tapped the phone of the National Security Adviser, Nuhu Ribadu.

Mr El-Rufai has pleaded not guilty to all charges, maintaining that his prosecution is politically motivated.

He remains in ICPC custody under court-authorised remand orders while his legal team challenges his continued detention.

Mr El-Rufai has been in ICPC detention since 18 February.

World.title: Benue seals two schools for forcing students to buy textbooks
World.content:
The Benue State Education Quality Assurance and Examinations Board (BEQAEB) has sealed two schools, Orenda and Opal, in Makurdi over alleged victimisation of students and violations of the state government’s textbook policy.

Jeffrey Adzam, an information officer with the board, disclosed this in a statement, saying the action followed complaints from parents and the schools’ alleged failure to comply with government directives on textbook purchases and reuse.

The board’s executive secretary, Terna Francis, led officials of its Directorate of Enforcement and Compliance to the schools, where a court order authorising the sealing of the premises was served on the proprietor before the facilities were locked.

According to the statement, the government’s textbook policy allows parents to reuse textbooks among their children and purchase approved books from external bookstores rather than being compelled to buy them directly from schools.

Mr Francis said the affected schools allegedly insisted that learners purchase textbooks from them, contrary to the policy.

He also said parents complained that some learners whose school fees had been paid but whose parents could not afford the prescribed textbooks were subjected to punitive treatment, including having their homework left unmarked.

The statement added that some parents who had already purchased the prescribed textbooks from external bookstores alleged that the schools refused to allow their children to use them.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

According to the complaints, the school management insisted that the parents either buy new textbooks directly from the schools or withdraw their children.

Mr Francis described the alleged practices as unacceptable, saying they undermined the welfare of learners and placed unnecessary financial pressure on parents.

Government directives

PREMIUM TIMES earlier reported on 7 September that the Benue State Government had issued directives prohibiting compulsory after-school lessons and restricting schools’ textbook practices for the 2026/2027 academic session.

The Commissioner for Education and Knowledge Management, Margaret Adamu, said Parent-Teacher Associations seeking to organise lessons outside regular school hours must obtain approval from the ministry and must not make the lessons compulsory.

Mrs Adamu also directed schools to use government-approved textbooks, prohibited restricted or customised non-transferable textbooks and said parents must be allowed to purchase approved books either from schools or other sources.

She further directed schools not to include textbook costs in school fees and warned that schools and individuals who violated the directives would face sanctions.

The latest action against Orenda and Opal schools follows complaints that the schools allegedly failed to comply with the textbook policy.

Court order

Mr Francis said the board had invited the proprietor and school administrators to a meeting to address the complaints, but they failed to honour the invitation.

He said BEQAEB subsequently approached the court through the state attorney-general and obtained an order authorising the sealing of the premises.

READ ALSO: Forgotten schoolchildren of Borno

The statement also alleged that the proprietor, Onyinye Okoye, and some staff members verbally assaulted the board’s officials after the court order was served and damaged a vehicle belonging to the board.

The allegations have not been independently verified.

The board condemned the reported incident, saying disputes with regulatory authorities should be resolved through lawful channels rather than violence or intimidation.

It said the schools would remain sealed until their proprietors and administrators met the board’s conditions and demonstrated compliance with government regulations, respect for court orders and commitment to protecting learners’ rights.

Mr Francis urged parents and guardians to submit formal petitions, supported by relevant evidence, when they experience similar alleged violations of education policies.

He said the board would investigate such complaints and take appropriate action in accordance with the law.

World.title: Court orders APC to conduct fresh primaries in 10 Plateau wards
World.content:
The Federal High Court in Jos, Plateau State, has ordered the All Progressives Congress (APC) to conduct fresh primary elections in 10 wards of the Jos South/Jos East Federal Constituency following a challenge to the process that produced Dachung Bagos as the party’s candidate for the 2027 general elections.

Justice Dorcas Agishi gave the order on Friday in a suit filed by Esther Danboyi against Mr Bagos, the APC and the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC).

The court also awarded ₦1.5 million in costs against the three defendants, directing each to pay ₦500,000 to Ms Danboyi.

The suit, marked FHC/J/CS/42/2026, challenged the validity of the APC primary over alleged non-compliance with the Constitution, the Electoral Act and the party’s guidelines for conducting primary elections.

According to Ms Danboyi’s lawyer, Ritji Yilwatda of Gyang Zi & Co., the court found that the required elections had not been conducted in the 10 wards challenged by his client.

He said the court consequently ordered that the affected elections be conducted within 30 days.

The affected wards are Du, Shen, Zawan ‘B’, Fobur ‘A’, Fobur ‘B’, Jarawan Kogi, Mai Juju/Doss, Federe, Shere East and Shere West.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Mr Yilwatda said his client had also complained that the APC denied her a fair hearing after she submitted petitions to the party and its Primary Election Appeal Committee over the disputed exercise.

He added that the court dismissed the preliminary objections and counter-affidavits filed by the defendants.

Dispute over APC primary

The lawsuit followed complaints by Ms Danboyi over the conduct of the APC primary that produced Mr Bagos as the party’s candidate for the federal constituency.

She challenged the process, alleging that the party failed to conduct valid elections in the affected wards and did not adequately address her petitions.

She asked the court to set aside the disputed results and compel the APC to conduct and conclude elections in wards where she alleged the exercise had not taken place.

The court’s reported findings on the 10 wards led to the order for fresh elections within 30 days.

The ruling introduces a new legal and political development in the APC’s preparations for the 2027 general elections in Jos South and Jos East.

World.title: 2027: Tinubu kicks off campaign in Kaduna 24 October – Yari
World.content:
President Bola Tinubu will begin his 2027 re-election campaign in Kaduna on 24 October.

The Director-General of the All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council, Abdulaziz Yari, announced this on Friday after meeting with the president at the Presidential Villa, Abuja.

Mr Yari, a former governor of Zamfara State and senator representing Zamfara West, said he has approved the timetable for the campaign.

He said the council would hold its inaugural meeting on 14 October at the State House Banquet Hall in Abuja.

“The President asked for me to come and brief him on where we are, and to discuss the timetable for the state visits,” he told State House correspondents.

“The inaugural meeting is going to be done on the 14th of this month. That’s next Wednesday at the State House banquet hall, and by God’s grace, on the 24th of October, we’re going to do our flag-off campaign in Kaduna, inshallah.”

He said the campaign team would subsequently visit Port Harcourt, Rivers State, and Maiduguri, Borno State.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

According to him, the full schedule of state visits, which Mr Tinubu has approved, will be released after the council’s inauguration.

Yari dismisses Atiku, Obi’s chances

Speaking on the chances of former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar and former Anambra State Governor Peter Obi in the 2027 presidential election, Mr Yari argued that neither had sufficient political support across northern and southern Nigeria to defeat Mr Tinubu.

He questioned whether Mr Obi could claim control of any state in northern Nigeria or whether the opposition could demonstrate comparable strength in the South.

Mr Yari maintained that a presidential candidate needed support in both regions to win an election.

He cited former President Muhammadu Buhari, who unsuccessfully contested three presidential elections before winning in 2015, arguing that his earlier defeats showed the difficulty of winning without sufficient support in southern Nigeria.

The senator claimed that Mr Tinubu currently enjoyed political control of more than 10 states each in the North and South.

“This is calculation, it is not rocket science,” he said.

He also defended the president’s economic policies, saying the administration had improved the situation it inherited in 2023.

“We are not promising. We are doing it, and we are going to continue,” he said.

The planned Kaduna event comes as political parties prepare for the 2027 general elections.

Under the Independent National Electoral Commission’s revised timetable, public campaigns for the presidential and National Assembly elections commenced on 19 August 2026, while the presidential election is scheduled for 16 January 2027.

World.title: Abducted Kogi councillor dies in captivity
World.content:
Suspected kidnappers have killed Rosemary Adukwu, a councillor representing Ogugu Ward III in Olamaboro Local Government Area of Kogi State, days after abducting her while she was travelling to Onitsha, Anambra State, to buy goods for her business.

Ms Adukwu was reportedly abducted on 30 September when the commercial vehicle she was travelling in was ambushed around Oji River, near the boundary between Enugu and Anambra states.

The assailants reportedly dragged her out of the vehicle and took her to an undisclosed location in a forest, leaving the other passengers unharmed.

The Chairman of Olamaboro Local Government Area, Ameh Williams, announced her death in a statement on Friday.

“It is with deep sorrow that we announce the sudden demise of our dear sister and colleague, Hon. Mrs. Rosemary Adukwu, the honourable councillor representing the good people of Ogugu Ward III in the eighth Olamaboro Legislative Council,” the statement read.

Mr Williams said her death was confirmed on Thursday while she was still in captivity.

Family raises concerns

The deceased’s family has raised concerns about the circumstances surrounding her abduction and death, alleging that the kidnappers singled her out from the other passengers and did not contact the family to demand a ransom before her death was reported.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

A family source, according to Daily Trust, said Ms Adukwu regularly travelled with the same driver to Onitsha to restock her business.

According to the source, she left for the market on 30 September after confirming with the driver that trading would take place the following day.

“At the boundary community between Enugu and Anambra states, precisely around Oji River, their vehicle ran into a barricade mounted by some people. Thereafter, the hoodlums dragged only her out of the vehicle and took her to an unknown destination. The other passengers continued their journey untouched,” the newspaper quoted the source.

The source said the family became concerned when the abductors failed to contact them for almost a week to demand a ransom.

The family subsequently contacted security operatives, who reportedly tracked the councillor’s phone number.

“On Thursday, a voice announced while receiving the call that the owner of the phone is dead,” the source said.

The source added that the driver and the person who answered the call to the councillor’s phone had been arrested and were assisting security operatives with the investigation.

PREMIUM TIMES could not independently verify the family’s account of the circumstances surrounding the abduction and death.

Community condemns killing

The President-General of the Ogugu District Union, Samuel Agada, condemned the abduction and killing, describing the incident as barbaric.

In a statement issued alongside the union’s national executive, Mr Agada said Ms Adukwu was a grassroots leader, businesswoman, wife and mother whose death had devastated her family and community.

READ ALSO: Police arrest Unilorin lecturer over social media post on Kogi road project

“Hon. Adukwu was a dedicated grassroots leader, a hardworking businesswoman and a devoted mother and wife who was only striving to earn a living for her family,” he said.

“This is a painful loss not only to her family and Ogugu Ward III, but to Ubelr District, Ogugu Chiefdom, Olamaboro LGA and Kogi State at large. We condemn this barbaric act in its totality.”

The councillor was reportedly buried at about 1 p.m. on Friday at her family compound in Ogugu Centre.

The spokesperson for the Kogi State Police Command, Saliu Oyiza Afusat, did not respond to enquiries about the incident as of the time of filing this report.

World.title: Negative perceptions keeping youths out of military – Soludo
World.content:
Gov. Chukwuma Soludo of Anambra State says negative public perceptions of the military and other security agencies sometimes discourage young people from joining the services.

Soludo spoke on Friday at the memorial service for the late Lt.-Gen. Chikadibia Obiakor (rtd.) at Alex Ekwueme Square, Awka.

He said the exemplary lives of officers such as Obiakor could inspire younger generations to embrace military service and other forms of national service.

The governor urged community leaders and elders to maintain close relationships with their people and serve as role models for younger generations.

“We must multitask and become the villager as a way of inspiring and motivating the younger ones,” he said.

Soludo described Obiakor as an illustrious son of Anambra whose distinguished military career and international peacekeeping service brought honour to Nigeria.

“We have come to celebrate the life of one of our best,” he said.

He described the late general as “Anambra’s export to Nigeria and the world”, noting his global service in promoting peace and maintaining law and order.

However, Soludo stressed that an individual’s greatest achievement lay in the positive impact made on their immediate community.

“The impact on the community is the most important impact; his people were able to testify that he was good,” he said.

The Chief of Defence Staff, Gen. Olufemi Oluyede, expressed condolences to the Obiakor family and joined people of Anambra and Nigeria in mourning the late officer.

Oluyede was represented by Maj.-Gen. Tariweriye Gagariga, Director-General of the Nigerian Army Heritage and Future Centre.

He described Obiakor as a decorated veteran whose distinguished service brought honour and dignity to the Nigerian Armed Forces.

Earlier, the deceased’s son, Mr Nonso Obiakor, reflected on his father’s life, highlighting his discipline, international peacekeeping commitment and dedication to humanity.

The memorial service attracted family members, senior military officers, government officials and other mourners celebrating Obiakor’s contributions to Anambra, Nigeria and the international community. (NAN)

World.title: Trump sows doubt on plan to livestream US military execution
World.content:
Photo by Kevin Dietsch / GETTY IMAGES NORTH AMERICA / Getty Images via AFP.

US President Donald Trump cast doubt Friday on whether authorities will livestream the firing squad execution of the perpetrator of a deadly attack on American soldiers, a plan that has drawn broad and bipartisan condemnation.

Nidal Hasan’s execution — scheduled for December 3 at Fort Hood, Texas, where he gunned down 13 people in 2009 — is set to be the first by a US military firing squad since 1945.

A Pentagon official told AFP on Thursday that the execution would be streamed live, after US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said “we’ll make sure that people are able to watch it, that it’s public.”

But Trump, who supports the death penalty in this case, left uncertain whether the execution would be publicly broadcast.

“They are making a determination about that, but he will be killed,” Trump said. “I really don’t care how he goes, as long as he goes.”

Earlier Friday, Vice President JD Vance told journalists who asked about the planned livestream that he does not “know that that’s actually going to happen.”

“This is a guy who committed, in my view, the worst terrorist attack on American soil outside of 9/11,” Vance said, but added that if the execution is broadcast live, “I’m not going to be watching it.”

Representative Austin Scott of Trump’s Republican Party said he supported executing Hasan but “livestreaming executions is what jihadists do. America is better than that.”

Senator Mark Kelly, a Democrat on the Senate Armed Services Committee, said Hasan should “face justice” but that public executions are “the kind of thing Iran and the Taliban do. Is this who we want to be associated with?”

Tech firms YouTube, Meta and X did not immediately respond to requests for comment on whether they would allow the execution to be streamed on their platforms.

TikTok directed AFP to its policy banning depictions of “graphic incidents and violence” including “the shooting of an individual.”

The UN High Commissioner for Human Rights condemned the plan, saying in a message sent to AFP on Friday that “the livestreaming of an execution is tantamount to a public execution and would breach the absolute prohibition of torture.”

Archbishop Paul Coakley, president of the US Conference of Catholic Bishops, said it was a “barbaric promotion of a culture of death and must be reconsidered.”

– ‘Compound the cruelty’ –

Hegseth said it would be the military’s first firing squad execution since World War II.

“People need to understand that…there’s serious consequence for these types of things,” Hegseth said in a video shared Thursday on official Pentagon X accounts.

The last US military execution was carried out in 1961, when John Bennett was hanged for rape and attempted murder.

The Death Penalty Information Center says 135 troops have been executed by the US military since 1916.

According to rights group Amnesty International, at least 17 public executions are known to have been carried out in 2025 — six in Afghanistan and 11 in Iran.

Amnesty’s Justin Mazzola said Friday that the death penalty is “a violation of human rights,” and that streaming Hasan’s execution “would only compound the cruelty.”

Twelve of the 13 people Hasan killed and 30 of those he wounded were soldiers. He was shot by a civilian police officer who responded to the attack and is paralyzed from the waist down.

Hasan chose to conduct his own defense during the trial but called no witnesses and gave no testimony, and made no attempt to deny the charges.

He was sentenced to death by a military jury in 2013.

Court-appointed defense attorneys expressed concern that he was seeking execution.

The court that convicted Hasan was told he was opposed to the US military’s occupations of Iraq and Afghanistan, and that he had spoken online with an alleged Al-Qaeda figure, radical cleric Anwar al-Awlaki, an American citizen subsequently killed in a US drone strike in Yemen.

World.title: My wife knew I dated actresses, yet didn’t fight them – Yinka Quadri
World.content:
Yoruba actor Yinka Quadri has revealed how his wife, Sadiat, treated female colleagues he was romantically involved with, saying she remained friendly with them despite knowing about his relationships.

The veteran actor disclosed this in an interview with African A List on YouTube, where he recounted how some actresses would approach his wife to discuss his romantic affairs with other women in the movie industry.

The actor met Sadiat in 1985 and they got married in 1989. They have children and grandchildren.

According to Quadri, his wife knew about his relationships with some of the same actresses who sometimes gossiped about him, but she never confronted them.

“At some point, some female colleagues in the industry will approach my wife to gossip that I’m dating other actresses, even though I’m also dating some of the very actresses who gossip about me. My wife knows about it and doesn’t fight with them,” he said.

Quadri also disclosed that Sadiat would accommodate and care for some of the actresses when they visited their home after late-night movie productions, despite knowing about their relationships with him.

“Sometimes, when we finish production late and some of them come to sleep at my house, my wife feeds and takes care of them despite knowing that I’m dating them,” he said.

The full interview will go live at 5 pm on Saturday.

World.title: Police arrest inspector, two civil guards over extortion in Imo
World.content:
By Emmanuel Iheaka

The Imo State Police Command has arrested a police traffic warden, Inspector Chinwe Ejiogu, and two personnel of the State Civil Guard Corps over alleged extortion and harassment of a motorist in Owerri.

The arrests followed the circulation of a viral video showing the officers allegedly harassing and attempting to extort a motorist who was said to be driving without a driver’s licence.

In a statement signed by the state Police Public Relations Officer, DSP Henry Okoye, the command condemned the conduct captured in the video, describing it as unacceptable and contrary to the standards of discipline and integrity expected of law enforcement personnel.

Okoye identified the police inspector as Ejiogu, attached to the Shell Camp Divisional Police Headquarters, while the two civil guard personnel were identified as Kelechi Nzediagwu and Onyedikachi Chibuike.

He said the three suspects were being detained at the State Criminal Investigation Department (SCID) as investigations continued.

“The Imo State Police Command is aware of a viral video in which a police traffic warden and two personnel of the State Civil Guard Corps were captured harassing and extorting a motorist allegedly driving without a driver’s licence in Owerri on October 8, 2026,” the statement said.

According to Okoye, the Commissioner of Police in the state, CP Audu Garba Bosso, has directed the command’s Complaint Response Unit (CRU) to investigate the incident.

The command also urged the affected motorist to report to the unit and provide relevant information to assist the investigation.

It said appropriate disciplinary action would be taken upon the conclusion of the investigation.

The police reiterated that no traffic violation justified extortion, harassment or abuse of office, warning personnel to discharge their duties in accordance with the law and treat members of the public with respect.

The command further urged members of the public to report incidents of police misconduct through the appropriate channels, assuring them that allegations of misconduct would be treated seriously.

World.title: Just In: Lagos varsity lecturers suspend strike
World.content:
By Victor Ahiuma-Young

Lecturers under the Academic Staff Union of Universities, ASUU, in three Lagos State-owned universities have suspended their industrial action and are set to return to classrooms with immediate effect.

The development has brought relief to students and parents affected by the disruption of academic activities.

The affected institutions are Lagos State University, LASU, Lagos State University of Education, LASUED, and Lagos State University of Science and Technology, LASUSTECH.

The unions announced the suspension on Friday, while expressing appreciation to the media, civil society organisations, CSOs, traditional rulers, students, parents and other stakeholders for their support throughout the negotiations. It said the collective efforts of these groups contributed significantly to the negotiation process, which centred on improved staff welfare and the implementation of outstanding academic agreements.

In a statement jointly issued by Olusegun Babalola, Coordinator, Steering Committee, ASUU-LASU; Grace Abimbola, Acting Chairman, ASUU-LASUED; and Murisiku Onigemo, Chairman, ASUU-LASUTECH, the unions said: “Following the official suspension of our industrial action today, the leadership and entire membership of the Academic Staff Union of Universities, ASUU, in Lagos State-owned universities wish to express our profound gratitude to the general public, institutional leaders, and key stakeholders who stood firmly by us throughout the negotiation process.

“Our struggle for improved staff welfare and the implementation of vital academic agreements has reached a significant milestone, largely due to the collective support of well-meaning individuals and organisations. We wish to express our deepest appreciation to the following:

“The Press and Broadcasting Organisations: We thank you for your objective, timely, and investigative coverage. Your platforms ensured that our grievances were accurately communicated to the public and policymakers, helping to keep the discussions balanced and constructive.

“Civil Society Organisations (CSOs): We are grateful for the solidarity, advocacy, and unwavering commitment to social justice demonstrated by the Joint Action Front (JAF), Education Rights Concern (ERC), Campaign for Democratic Workers Rights (CDWR), and other pro-worker organisations. Your defense of quality public tertiary education provided valuable support for our cause.

“Our Revered Traditional Rulers: We honour our royal fathers for their timely interventions, fatherly counsel, and behind-the-scenes diplomatic efforts. Your wisdom helped bridge communication gaps during critical moments of the impasse.

“Students, Parents, and Other Stakeholders: We deeply appreciate your resilience, patience, and understanding throughout this period. We recognise the sacrifices you have made and reaffirm that our struggle remains focused on securing improved staff welfare and a better future for public university education in Lagos State.

“As our members return to the classrooms with immediate effect, we reaffirm our commitment to academic excellence and quality university education. We also look forward to continued engagement with the Lagos State Government to ensure the full resolution of all outstanding issues relating to our welfare package.

“Once again, we appreciate everyone who stood with us throughout this struggle. Your solidarity and support have been invaluable.”

World.title: Passengers groan as flight delays, cancellations worsen
World.content:
By Dickson Omobola

Domestic air travellers are lamenting frequent flight delays and cancellations across airports in the country, with many expressing frustration over prolonged waiting times and disrupted travel plans.

Saturday Vanguard also observed that departure halls at several airports across the country have been crowded in recent times, with many stranded and delayed passengers wearing long faces.

A visit to the domestic terminals of the Murtala Muhammed Airport, Lagos, Monday, lent credence to the development, as passengers waited for updates on delayed flights.

At the domestic terminal of the Nnamdi Azikiwe Airport, Abuja, Tuesday, the departure hall was crowded, with travellers expressing concern over the frequency of flight disruptions.

For instance, one of the passengers, Eze, said his flight had been delayed both on his journey from Lagos to Abuja and on his return trip.

He said: “My flight was delayed while I was going to Abuja from Lagos. It was delayed as I am returning. I am stressed, honestly. And I am not alone. Delay announcements are many, about four in two hours today. Terrible.”

Another passenger, Jeremiah, whose flight from Warri to Lagos was disrupted, Sunday, said he was forced to spend additional money after the flight was rescheduled to the following day.

He said: “I had to part away with another money after my flight scheduled for 5pm on Sunday was shifted to the next day. I needed to be in Lagos by 9am on Monday because I had an important meeting to attend.”

Recently, a passenger, Segalink, also took to X, formerly Twitter, to express frustration over a prolonged delay on an Air Peace flight from Asaba to Lagos.

He wrote: “Air Peace is interesting. Flight P47863 from Asaba to Lagos which was scheduled to depart at 15:00 on 26/09/2026 (yesterday) kept being rescheduled allegedly due to maintenance and the majority of the passengers slept at the airport in the hope of flying only to be told around 12am that they would fly by 5am this morning.

“Unfortunately, that promise wasn’t fulfilled until almost 9am today. These were passengers who bought tickets for a 10am flight originally from Asaba to Lagos. No refreshments or hotel accommodation were provided. Is this how we will continue? These are folks who will not permit you to board if you are 15 minutes late to the counter.”

Recall that the Nigeria Civil Aviation Authority, NCAA’s, Summary of Domestic Airline Flight Disruptions Operations for August, which showed that domestic airlines collectively recorded 4,801 disruptions out of 7,961 operated flights.

Air Peace recorded the highest number of disruptions, with 1,337 delayed or cancelled flights out of 1,864 operated during the month. United Nigeria Airlines delayed or cancelled 951 of its 1,231 operated flights, while Enugu State-owned Enugu Air recorded 586 disruptions out of 878 operated flights. ValueJet disrupted 438 of its 767 operated flights.

Akwa Ibom State-owned Ibom Air recorded 257 disruptions out of 560 operated flights, while Arik operated 301 flights, of which 188 were delayed and one was cancelled.

However, the airlines faulted the statistics, saying most of the disruptions were caused by factors beyond their control.

World.title: We’ll make it difficult for Amaechi to campaign in Rivers if… – Wike
World.content:
Wike

By Omeiza Ajayi

ABUJA: Minister of the Federal Capital Territory FCT, Nyesom Wike, has warned that it will be difficult for former Minister of Transportation, Rotimi Amaechi, running mate to the African Democratic Congress ADC presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, to campaign in Rivers State if he continues to attack President Bola Tinubu and his supporters.

Wike spoke on Friday in Abuja after a meeting with the chairmen of the six area councils of the FCT. He was reacting to comments credited to Amaechi, who allegedly said only thieves and mad people would vote for Tinubu.

“If he continues this line, it will be difficult for him to campaign in Rivers. We will not take that. If security agencies and INEC can fold their hands, that’s their business, but we will not allow it,” Wike said.

Wike said the remarks were aired on television, and that they went further to include Edo people.

“All of us watched on television yesterday where he said it’s only thieves that can vote for Bola Ahmed Tinubu, only mad people can vote for Bola Ahmed Tinubu, and that if Edo people vote for him, it means Edo people are mad. This is supposedly a vice presidential candidate of a political party seeking to take over power,” he said.

The minister said agencies such as the Independent National Electoral Commission INEC should sanction politicians who engage in personality attacks instead of issue-based campaigns.

“You see one problem we have in this country is that agencies or commissions should be able to take their functions seriously. Many Nigerians have called INEC to sanction political parties, candidates, or some politicians who, in their campaigns, incite the public or raise matters that are not issue-based,” he said.

Wike then challenged Amaechi to account for projects executed while he was governor of Rivers State.

“I have challenged him to tell Nigerians where is our $39 million cassava flour mill which you claimed you built? Where is the $10 million you paid to a Cuban company to fumigate Rivers State so there will be no mosquito bite? Where is the N68 billion monorail? Where is the $308 million you sold our gas turbine?

“Amaechi has looted the treasury. Ask him why he was indicted by a Judicial Panel of Inquiry and why he went to court to challenge that indictment and lost at the Supreme Court,” Wike alleged.

World.title: Trump appoints ‘devoted fan’ Katie Zacharia as press secretary
World.content:
US President Donald Trump on Friday announced the appointment of conservative commentator Katie Zacharia as his new White House press secretary, praising her as a loyal supporter.

“She has an unblemished record of support, and has been a loyal and brilliant supporter, right from the beginning,” Trump posted on his Truth Social platform.

“She is, likewise, a devoted fan and member of MAGA!” he added, referring to his Make America Great Again movement.

Zacharia, a lawyer and communications adviser to Trump’s media company, will succeed Karoline Leavitt, who stepped down in August after becoming one of the most prominent public faces of his second administration.

Trump hailed his new spokeswoman’s credentials, including her work for his presidential campaigns, and said he was confident she would enjoy a good relationship with the White House press corps.

Zacharia, in a post on X, thanked Trump for the “distinguished privilege of serving as White House Press Secretary.”

Trump’s “confidence is a true privilege, and his leadership is a blessing to this country,” she wrote.

“The work ahead is to continue delivering strong results for our Country and communicating to the American people the major wins that this Administration is making every single day.”

Zacharia currently serves as a senior communications advisor to Trump Media and Technology Group, which operates the president’s Truth Social platform.
