World.title: Ex-justice chancellor: Orthodox church has slim chance in European court
World.content:
Ex-justice chancellor Allar Jõks says the Estonian Christian Orthodox Church and Pühtitsa Convent have little chance in European court after filing a complaint prematurely.

The Estonian Christian Orthodox Church (EKÕK) and Pühtitsa Convent have challenged amendments to Estonia's Churches and Congregations Act that require them to sever ties with the Russian Orthodox Church by December 28.

Jõks said the rules for bringing a case before the European Court of Human Rights (ECtHR) are very strict: applicants must first exhaust all domestic legal remedies and show that their rights have actually been violated.

"The ECtHR does not assess laws in the abstract to determine whether they comply with the European Convention on Human Rights, much less issue advance rulings on how they should be applied," he explained.

As both the EKÕK and Pühtitsa Convent still have until late December to make the changes required by law, Jõks said it's too soon to conclusively determine whether either one's rights have been violated and, if so, whether they have exhausted all domestic legal remedies before turning to the European court.

Estonian court system skipped

The Interior Ministry cannot assess any changes until after the December 28 deadline. If it finds them insufficient, it can ask a district court to order the religious organizations' dissolution.

Even if dissolution proceedings begin, however, Jõks said the church would still have access to judicial review and the right to appeal, meaning the dispute could therefore pass through three levels of Estonia's court system.

If questions arise over the constitutionality of the Churches and Congregations Act, he continued, the case could also trigger a constitutional review, potentially leading to a different outcome from the Supreme Court's June 8 ruling upholding the legislation.

Metropolitan Eugene, head of the Estonian Orthodox Church of the Moscow Patriarchate (MPEÕK). Source: Priit Mürk/ERR

Jõks said the EKÕK and Pühtitsa Convent's premature complaint to the ECtHR thus appears to signal distrust of the Estonian judicial system.

"Anyone who agrees with that line of thinking should try testing the judicial system on the other side of the Narva River," he said, referring to Russia.

Six months to cut ties with Moscow

The Ministry of the Interior has given the Estonian Christian Orthodox Church, which remains affiliated with the Moscow Patriarchate, six months to appoint a new metropolitan and sever its ties with the Russian Orthodox Church.

Its previous leader, Metropolitan Eugene (legal name Valeri Reshetnikov), was ordered to leave Estonia in February 2024 after authorities refused to extend the Russian citizen's residence permit on national security grounds.

In its rejection, the Police and Border Guard Board (PPA) cited Reshetnikov's activities and public statements as a representative of the Moscow Patriarchate in Estonia.

The Estonian Internal Security Service (ISS) likewise said both he and Patriarch Kirill, the religious leader of the Russian Orthodox Church, had consistently supported Russia's war against Ukraine and helped advance the Kremlin's security policy in Estonia.

Formerly known as the Estonian Orthodox Church of the Moscow Patriarchate (MPEÕK), the Estonian Christian Orthodox Church (EKÕK) is separate from the Estonian Apostolic Orthodox Church (EAÕK), the legal continuation of the Estonian Orthodox Church (EÕK) under the Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople.

World.title: Estonia plans up to €5 million payments to municipalities that allow wind farms
World.content:
Minister of Energy Erkki Keldo has sent for approval a draft regulation that would create the possibility to pay local governments up to €5 million in support to encourage the construction of wind farms on their territory.

The purpose of the measure, called Tuulehoo preemia (Wind Speed Bonus), is to increase the readiness of local governments to carry out wind‑energy developments, especially in the most time‑consuming stages of planning and permit procedures, the Ministry of Climate said.

The maximum amount of support is up to five million euros per municipality, divided into two parts: the first part can be applied for after the planning has been established, and the second part once construction permits for the turbines have been issued. The right to apply for support arises when the established plans foresee at least five wind turbines.

According to the ministry's press release, the support can be used to improve local life — for example, renovating schools and other public buildings, building pedestrian and cycling paths, creating local energy and storage solutions, and improving crisis preparedness.

The total volume of the bonus support is at least 12 million euros, planned for 2027 and 2028. The measure will be financed from the sale of emission allowances (CO₂ quotas) up to 12 million euros and from the state budget.

The bonus does not mean that a municipality must establish a wind‑farm plan or issue a construction permit. All existing requirements remain in force: necessary studies and environmental impact assessments must be carried out, and local residents must be involved, the ministry explained.

At the same time, it was added that the bonus payment does not replace the wind‑turbine fee. While the turbine fee provides local governments and residents with long‑term annual income throughout the wind farm's operating life, Tuulehoo preemia enables local benefits to arise earlier — at the planning and construction‑permit stage.

The Ministry of Climate expressed hope that the planned bonus will also contribute to the state's long‑term goal of increasing energy security and the share of clean energy, and ensuring affordable electricity prices.

"Onshore wind will be one of the most cost‑effective ways to produce electricity in the coming years, and it increases access to low electricity prices. To reduce dependence on fossil‑fuel imports, we need affordable, renewable, domestic production. Therefore, developing wind farms is of strategic importance, and we cannot allow the construction of new parks across Estonia to stall. This is why we are creating the bonus. The local community must feel that changes in their living environment bring them practical benefits. Developing wind farms should be cooperation that benefits everyone," Keldo said in the press release.

World.title: Estonia pushes firm to drop Russian supplier after EU strategic project nod
World.content:
Foreign Minister Margus Tsahkna (Eesti 200) expects NPM Silmet to set a deadline for ending the use of Russian raw materials as it receives EU backing for a major expansion.

The European Commission on Friday selected Silmet 2.0 as one of 46 new strategic projects for bolstering the EU's supply of critical raw materials. Tsahkna said the project must come with a firm deadline for ending the company's reliance on Russian raw materials.

"We will work with the European Commission to set a clear deadline for NPM Silmet to stop using Russian raw materials," he said, emphasizing that the company must move quickly to alternative suppliers as with strategic status comes responsibility.

"We cannot allow an industry critical to Europe's security to remain dependent on supplies from an aggressor state," the minister added.

Silmet 2.0 is an investment and development plan to adapt the Sillamäe-based plant's infrastructure and production processes to new raw material sources, allowing its strategically important output for Europe to continue.

Silmet magnets. Source: ERR

Alongside ramping up pressure on Russia via sanctions, Europe also has to strengthen its own production capacity and find new sources of supply, Tsahkna said, adding that the Silmet project would help bolster the EU's economic security.

"Estonia continues to support strong sanctions against Russia," he stressed.

Russian supplier dropped from sanctions package

Earlier this week, Estonia successfully pushed to exclude a Russian company that supplies rare earth metals to NPM Silmet from the EU's proposed 22nd sanctions package against Russia, which is awaiting formal approval.

The Foreign Ministry says NPM Silmet plays a crucial role in Europe's critical raw materials supply chain, with its products used in the electronics, medicine, automotive, aviation and defense industries.

EU strategic projects aim to secure supplies of critical raw materials and reduce reliance on third countries.

World.title: Taiwan’s leader says increasing defence spending to ‘deter war’
World.content:
Taipei – Taiwan aims to “deter war” by increasing its defence spending, the democratic island’s leader said on Saturday, as China uses military pressure to assert its territorial claims.

Taiwan’s 23 million people live under the constant threat of an attack by China, which insists the island is part of its territory and has threatened to use force to annex it.

“Our aim by increasing investment in national defence is not to provoke, rather, it is to deter war,” President Lai Ching-te said in a speech to celebrate Taiwan’s National Day.

Successive administrations have ramped up military spending as Taiwan improves its fighting abilities to avoid a potential Chinese invasion — and to show the United States it is serious about its own defence.

Lai’s government has earmarked a record NT$1.1 trillion (US$34.5 billion) in defence spending for 2027, which accounts for more than three percent of GDP.

“We do not seek hegemony, nor do we seek to dominate others,” Lai said in his annual address in front of the Presidential Office in Taipei, where thousands of people, including foreign diplomats, were gathered.

“However, peace cannot rely solely on wishes, and tolerance cannot become a pretext for aggressors to encroach ever further,” Lai said, noting that China continued to “apply pressure through military and grey-zone activities in an attempt to alter the status quo across the Taiwan Strait”.

Lai welcomed talks between the United States and China, but insisted “there must be respect for the right of the people of Taiwan to exist”.

Government officials in Washington and Taipei have said repeatedly that US policy on Taiwan has not changed under President Donald Trump, whose remarks have jangled nerves at times.

– ‘US support is extremely important’ –

The United States switched official diplomatic relations from Taipei to Beijing nearly 50 years ago, but Washington is Taipei’s most important security backer.

Trump’s suggestion in May, following a meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping in Beijing, that US arms sales to Taiwan could be a bargaining chip with China set off alarm bells across the world.

Taiwan is waiting for Trump’s signature on $14 billion worth of weapons, including the US-made Patriot air defence system.

Taiwanese fighter jets and two Chinook helicopters carrying giant Taiwan flags flew over the capital ahead of Lai’s wide-ranging speech, which also covered housing pressure and the declining population.

“You can really feel the warmth in Taiwanese society,” said Feng Jing-heng, 70, who was in the crowd watching the military parade and dance performances.

Tao Yi-feng, a political scientist at National Taiwan University, said Lai’s speech was “relatively moderate” and unlikely to be met with “overt reaction from Beijing”.

Saturday’s celebrations mark the 115th anniversary of the toppling of China’s Qing dynasty and the subsequent founding of the Republic of China.

The current dispute between China and Taiwan dates to a civil war between the nationalist forces of Chiang Kai-shek, who retreated to the island in 1949 after being defeated by Mao Zedong’s communist fighters.

Parliamentary speaker Han Kuo-yu, who is a senior member of the main opposition party that favours closer ties with China, said “US support is extremely important to Taiwan’s security”, but he noted the historical and cultural links with China.

“The overwhelming majority of Taiwanese compatriots do not want war; they wish to live their lives in peace and hope for peaceful cross-strait exchanges,” Han said at the National Day event.

World.title: Year later, Gaza ceasefire promises mostly unfulfilled
World.content:
Jerusalem – One year after US President Donald Trump declared the war in Gaza to be over, few of the long-term promises of the ceasefire have come to fruition.

Here is a list of some of the key points of the October 10, 2025 ceasefire and where things stand:

– Hostages released, calm in Israel –

Three days after the agreement was announced, Hamas freed the 20 remaining living hostages seized during the group’s October 7, 2023 attack, the deadliest day in Israel’s history.

The captives’ return was a key priority for Israel, whose public had agonised over their fate.

The ceasefire anniversary also marks one year of quiet for Israel from the Gaza front, with no rocket attacks by Hamas.

The group’s missile inventory was depleted by near-constant Israeli bombardment, which damaged or destroyed the vast majority of buildings in the Palestinian territory.

The US military set up a command post with foreign allies near the Gaza border to monitor the truce.

– No Israeli withdrawal or let-up –

Israel has reduced its level of attacks but has kept striking Gaza on a near-daily basis.

Israeli strikes have killed some 1,450 Palestinians since the ceasefire, according to Gaza’s health ministry, which operates under Hamas and whose figures are considered accurate by the United Nations.

Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who is in a tight election race, has vowed to kill everyone involved in the October 7 attack.

Netanyahu said on the attack’s anniversary that 4,000 out of 6,000 “Hamas monsters” had been killed.

Israeli forces were allowed to stay in 53 percent of Gaza under the terms of the ceasefire, but a year later they control about 70 percent of it, according to official accounts.

– Hamas remains, with weapons –

The second phase of the agreement was supposed to include a political transition away from Hamas, and technocrat Ali Shaath was appointed head of a new National Committee for the Administration of Gaza (NCAG).

Hamas announced in July that it was disbanding its governing body and handing over Gaza’s administration to the US-blessed NCAG.

But Hamas effectively remains in charge of security in Gaza, and Shaath has taken a low profile.

The Palestinian Islamist movement elected a new leader, Khalil al-Hayya, in July. Shortly afterwards, the group announced it would give up its weapons, a step hailed by Trump as a breakthrough.

But Israel has been sceptical, with Netanyahu demanding verifiable decommissioning of all weapons down to individual guns.

Hamas has not gone ahead with disarmament, and Israel has refused to reciprocate by starting to withdraw forces.

– Reconstruction just talk –

Trump set up a new global body for the deal dubbed the “Board of Peace”, tapping as key figures former British prime minister Tony Blair and Bulgarian diplomat Nickolay Mladenov, who serves as “Gaza high representative”.

Trump, a critic of foreign aid, in January promised $10 billion in US funding to the board he controls, and Gulf allies have pledged more, but no money is known to have made its way to Gaza reconstruction.

In September, the board proposed a $2.45 billion Gaza recovery plan at a meeting of its members and stakeholders, in an effort meant to span over six months.

World.title: Hunger and malnutrition stalk Gazans, a year on from ceasefire
World.content:
Khan Yunis – Every day, Gazan mother Niyaha al-Masri spends six exhausting hours or more queueing at a community kitchen in the hope of getting some food for her family.

It has been a year since a ceasefire between Hamas and Israel was supposed to allow food to flood into the ruined territory, yet widespread hunger persists there.

Masri has little choice. Without the kitchen run by humanitarian groups, she and her eight children would have “nothing at all”, the 35-year-old told AFP.

Each day she sets out early in the morning and returns in the afternoon, this time bringing four containers of rice, lentils and a little chicken, which the family throws itself at.

Among them is her husband, wounded in both legs by an airstrike, meaning he “cannot go and fight with the others” to get food.

This will be the only meal of the day for the family of 10, living in a tent in Khan Yunis. There was no breakfast and they will have no dinner.

What little flour they have, Masri explained, has to be rationed.

In August 2025, a United Nations-backed body, the IPC, declared a state of famine in Gaza, though Israel quickly denounced it as a lie.

By December, the UN had lifted that declaration, saying that the ceasefire had allowed in enough supplies over the course of two months to ease conditions.

COGAT, the Israeli defence ministry organisation responsible for civilian affairs in the Palestinian territories, told AFP that the humanitarian situation in Gaza was stable.

But Shaun Hughes, of the UN’s World Food Programme, was less sanguine.

The food security situation, he said, “is still extremely serious”.

The most recent figures, from July, show that “1.4 million out of the population of about 2.1 million people are acutely food insecure”, he said, with 200,000 of them “just one step below famine”.

– ‘Shameful’ –

While some food is getting in, a lack of sufficient nutritional variety continues to pose a health threat.

“Dietary diversity is a major food security issue in Gaza,” said Hughes.

“You cannot survive on dry goods and wheat flour and bread alone. Particularly children, particularly pregnant and breastfeeding mothers, they need the micronutrients that come with high protein foods, fresh vegetables, fresh fruits,” he explained.

Masri said that her children, aged between three and 14, “dream of eating fruit” but the family doesn’t have the means to buy any.

She said one of her sons suffered from malnutrition during the 2025 famine, although “little by little, his condition is improving”.

Malnutrition isn’t only caused by a lack of food, but also essential nutrients. It weakens the immune system of children, making them vulnerable to illnesses and stunting their growth.

“Repeated bouts of acute malnutrition amongst children is something that human beings just don’t recover from,” said Hughes.

Cognitive and physical impairments “continue into later life”, he added.

At Khan Yunis’s Nasser hospital, the head of the malnutrition unit, Israa al-Najjar, told AFP she had “observed an increase in syndromes and conditions” linked to malnutrition that affect the immune system.

In a report published on Thursday, the day after the third anniversary of the October 7 Hamas attack that sparked the Gaza war, Medecins du Monde published a study that found 93 percent of pregnant or breastfeeding women had symptoms of anaemia, which is closely linked to malnutrition.

Just 17 percent had a sufficiently varied diet to meet their nutritional needs, the group found.

All the while, Masri has kept visiting the community kitchen, despite asthma leaving her exhausted.

Her children spend their days collecting “pieces of nylon, bits of cardboard and chunks of foam” to try and reinforce their tent, which is in a poor state.

She said it was “shameful” that her children had to do so.

“I swear to God, this isn’t normal.”

World.title: Three Mexicans convicted in murders of Australian, US surfers
World.content:
Ensenada – A Mexican judge on Friday convicted three men in the 2024 murders of two Australian surfers and their American friend, who were killed during a botched robbery that sparked international outrage.

Australian brothers Jake and Callum Robinson, aged 30 and 33, respectively, and their friend Carter Rhoad, 30, were on a surfing trip to Mexico’s Pacific coast when they were shot dead in Baja California state in a suspected robbery.

They were camping in a remote beachside area near the coastal city of Ensenada when they were attacked on April 27, 2024.

Their bodies were found days later, dumped in a cliff-top shaft, with gunshot wounds to their heads.

The judge ruled that the three Mexican defendants acted with premeditation. They have yet to be sentenced.

The Robinsons’ parents traveled from Australia for the month-long trial.

Debra Robinson burst into tears when the guilty verdict was pronounced.

In a statement on behalf of the family Martin Robinson said that “while no verdict can ever bring back our boys or ease the heartbreak of losing them” the convictions marked “an important step towards justice and accountability.”

The prosecution has requested 210 years imprisonment for each of the accused, though the maximum sentence in Baja California is 60 years.

– Victim begged for mercy –

In its closing arguments on Thursday, the prosecution described the cold-blooded killings of the three surfers, who were caught off guard at their campsite.

A 9mm and a .45 caliber pistol were used in the attack.

The prosecutors recalled the testimony of the girlfriend of the main suspect, identified only as Jesus Gerardo, at her trial last November.

She said that Rhoad had begged for his life and that her boyfriend, who is nicknamed “El Kekas,” had bragged about “how beautifully” the victims cried and about items he robbed from them.

The girlfriend was sentenced to two decades in prison after admitting that she instigated the robbery in order to steal the pickup’s tires.

Testifying on the final day of the trial, Debra Robinson said what hurt herself and her husband the most was that “in their final hours” their sons “were treated with such cruelty.”

Rhoad’s fiancee Natalie Weirtz told the court by video call that the accused “must be punished so that no other family suffers the same pain.”

Baja California is one of Mexico’s most violent states, plagued by organized crime and drug trafficking, although cartel activity doesn’t usually affect tourists.

Other foreign visitors have been targeted in attacks on Mexico’s Pacific coast.

Two Australian surfers, Dean Lucas and Adam Coleman, were murdered in 2015 while traveling through the northwestern state of Sinaloa. Their bodies were later burned.

World.title: Trump hails Russia deal to release diesel as midterms loom
World.content:
Washington – US President Donald Trump said Friday that he had secured Russia’s agreement for a major release of diesel, as he eased war sanctions on Moscow in a push to lower energy costs ahead of midterm elections.

Moscow has been hit with waves of sanctions by the United States and partners since its 2022 invasion of neighboring Ukraine, and President Volodymyr Zelensky criticized Trump for an “unworthy” and “weak” move.

The deal comes weeks before key US elections where Trump’s Republican Party risks losing its grip on Congress as voters express frustration over the mounting cost of living.

Prices at US gasoline and diesel pumps have surged since late February, when US-Israel strikes targeting Iran triggered Tehran’s blockage of the Strait of Hormuz, a critical waterway for energy transit.

“Russia will immediately supply over 300,000 Tons of Diesel Fuel to the American and Global Marketplace,” Trump said on social media after talks with Russian leader Vladimir Putin.

The Kremin said Russia “reaffirmed its readiness to supply oil and oil products to the American and world markets.”

Trump added Moscow would supply 500,000 tons in November, followed by one million tons, with further larger releases promised.

Zelensky told reporters: “It is certainly not honest, it is certainly unworthy of our partners, and it is, in my view, a weak decision.”

The US Treasury issued a temporary license Friday to enable Russian diesel to flow to global markets through April 2027.

“Lower prices for Americans, especially our Great Farmers, Ranchers, and Truckers, is my Greatest Priority,” Trump posted on social media.

– Conflict stalemate –

The average cost of regular US gasoline has jumped more than 46 percent since late February to $4.37 per gallon, while that of diesel rocketed 67 percent over the same period to $6.28 per gallon.

Trump has blamed Ukrainian strikes on Russian refineries for surging fuel prices, although the US-Israeli war with Iran has been the principal disruptor of global energy supplies.

News of the deal came as Ukrainian and US negotiators met on Friday in Miami in a fresh attempt to break the conflict’s stalemate.

The sides “held constructive discussions on potential avenues to de-escalate and conclude the war with Russia ahead of winter,” said US envoy Steve Witkoff.

The Miami meeting follows visits to Moscow and Kyiv last month by Witkoff, a longtime Trump confidant, and Jared Kushner, the president’s son-in-law, as Washington seeks to revive negotiations that have yielded little progress.

With winter approaching, the prospect of continued fighting and attacks on vital infrastructure has added urgency to the search for a settlement against a backdrop of deadly Russian attacks.

On Thursday a Russian strike on buses in the frontline Ukrainian city of Kramatorsk killed 30 people.

Trump’s repeated attempts to broker an end to the war have foundered over Moscow’s sweeping territorial demands, particularly its insistence on controlling all of Ukraine’s eastern Donbas region, including areas still held by Kyiv.

Zelensky has rejected surrendering Ukrainian-held territory, warning that Russia could use it as a springboard for another attack.

Russia now occupies roughly one-fifth of Ukrainian territory.

The Miami discussions covered “security guarantees, as well as longer-term arrangements for Ukraine’s and Europe’s security to prevent future conflicts, and support Ukraine’s post-war reconstruction,” Witkoff said.

Officials from Britain, France and Germany were at the talks, along with representatives of NATO and the European Union.

World.title: Anthropic AI model sent fake murder tip to Philadelphia police
World.content:
San Francisco – An artificial intelligence model developed by Anthropic submitted a fabricated tip about an unsolved homicide to Philadelphia police, authorities said Friday, criticizing the company for taking two months to report the incident.

The Philadelphia Police Department said the false submission was made in July through PhillyUnsolvedMurders.com, a public website where people can share information about unsolved killings.

According to Anthropic’s account, as relayed by police, the model was running a test that involved interacting with randomly selected websites when it reached the site and filed false information about an unsolved murder.

The AI model presented itself as someone who might have knowledge of the case.

The department said it was going public with the incident ahead of a report that Anthropic was planning to release Friday describing this and other instances of unintended behavior by its models.

The case echoed other recent cases, including one where an OpenAI agent undergoing a security evaluation broke out of its testing environment and breached systems at AI platform Hugging Face.

The episode heightened concerns about the AI industry’s increased use of AI agents, systems programmed to take multi-step actions without human supervision.

Anthropic did not immediately respond to a request from AFP for comment.

Police said the tip, dated July 18, was flagged as spam and never reached the department’s Real-Time Crime Center for vetting.

They added that there was no sign that police systems had been breached or department data compromised.

Anthropic discovered the incident on September 28, shut down the automated testing process responsible and added a new validation step for future tests, police said.

The company alerted the department on October 7, and the two sides met the following day.

“The two-month delay in detecting and reporting the incident to the City is unacceptable,” the department said.

Police said their safeguards had limited the impact, but that these “do not diminish the seriousness of an AI system presenting fabricated information as though it came from a person with knowledge of a homicide.”

“Unsolved cases involve real victims, grieving families and investigators working to secure answers,” the statement added.

World.title: Flydubai co-pilot planned suicide attack on Tel Aviv airport: UAE prosecutor
World.content:
Dubai – The co-pilot who attacked the captain of a flydubai jet last month had planned to crash the plane into Tel Aviv’s international airport, the United Arab Emirates’ top prosecutor said on Friday.

The unnamed Omani co-pilot, now in custody in the UAE, had drawn inspiration from Al-Qaeda’s September 11, 2001 suicide attacks on the United States, and carried out his attempt “with the aim of causing the greatest possible loss of life”, according to the prosecutor’s findings published by state media.

“The findings showed that he had met the professional and security requirements for employment, including holding a pilot’s licence, providing a certificate of good conduct and completing the required checks.”

“However, none of the procedures revealed any indications of his extremist views or his intention to carry out a terrorist plot.”

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu previously said that the co-pilot must have got around restrictions preventing individuals from nations that do not recognise Israel operating flights to the country.

According to the UAE prosecutor, the co-pilot — identified in reports as Hamam al-Hammami — had previously worked for Oman Air and Royal Air Maroc.

– ‘Extremist literature’ –

Last week, Emirati investigators said the co-pilot was planning a terrorist attack and revealed that he had used the cockpit’s emergency axe to attack the captain, but did not at the time reveal his motivations.

Netanyahu told the media last week that the suspect had undergone “Islamist radical indoctrination”.

According to the Emirati prosecutor, the co-pilot was radicalised while studying in Australia “through reading extremist literature and following online content glorifying terrorist organisations and suicide attacks”.

He said this was the co-pilot’s third flight to Tel Aviv, following two earlier trips he had used to plan the attack.

During the flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv, the Omani co-pilot assaulted the plane’s Indian captain, Smit Machchhar, but he managed to open the cockpit door, allowing passengers and crew to overpower the attacker and force an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia.

In the immediate aftermath, passengers described rushing the cockpit and a fight for control after the plane suddenly plunged by around 5,000 metres (17,000 feet).

An off-duty pilot travelling on the plane was then able to take the controls and land the aircraft safely in Saudi Arabia.

The passengers on board the aircraft were overwhelmingly Israeli, with Netanyahu hailing them and the pilot for their bravery after the foiled attack.

He later ordered a “thorough review of all security aspects of foreign civil aviation to Israel” in response to the incident.

World.title: Mike Ditka: Chicago Bears icon as player and coach
World.content:
Los Angeles – Mike Ditka was already an NFL champion and Chicago icon when he guided the celebrated 1985 Bears to the Super Bowl crown.

With Ditka’s death on Friday at age 86, his legendary role on one of the most overwhelming teams in NFL history was recalled fondly by American football fans.

Coached by Ditka, led by quarterback Jim McMahon and featuring legendary running back Walter Payton and unlikely superstar William “Refrigerator” Perry,” the 1985 Bears also boasted one of the best defenses in NFL history. They lost just one game before pounding the New England Patriots 46-10 in Super Bowl 20.

Their on-field dominance was matched by an off-field swagger that earned them pop-culture fame reaching far beyond traditional NFL supporters.

“They changed the laws of football,” former US President Barack Obama — who calls Chicago home — said of the team. “They were gritty. They were gutsy. They were hard-working. They were fun-loving.”

For Ditka, born Michael Dyczko in the Pittsburgh-area town of Carnegie, Pennsylvania, on October 18, 1939, grit, guts and hard work had long been the keys to gridiron success.

“There’s more to winning than just wanting to,” Ditka once said. “You have to prove yourself every Sunday. “Just throwing your helmet on the field doesn’t scare anyone.

“There’s no more empty feeling in the world than losing.”

Drafted fifth overall by the Bears in 1961, Ditka introduced a new dimension to the tight end position long the preserve of talented blockers.

He was among the first tight ends to emerge as a significant pass receiving threat, punishing opposing defenses with 56 catches for 1,076 yards and 12 touchdowns in his Rookie of the Year ’61 season.

In 1964, he caught 75 passes — a season record for tight ends that lasted until 1980.

He earned All-NFL honors four straight seasons from 1961 through 1964 and was a Pro Bowl choice after each of his first five seasons.

Ditka finished his 12-year playing career with 427 receptions for 5,812 yards and 43 touchdowns and was inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame as a player in 1988.

By then, he had left Chicago and returned in triumph.

After a falling out with Chicago owner-coach George Halas, Ditka was traded to the Eagles in 1967, and finished his playing career with Dallas.

His best campaign with the Cowboys came in 1971, when they won their first Super Bowl title.

Ditka had 30 receptions that year and he scored the final touchdown in the Cowboys’ 24-3 win over the Miami Dolphins in Super Bowl Six.

Ditka was an assistant coach for the Cowboys when they won the Super Bowl in 1978.

– Folk hero –

In 1982, Halas brought Ditka back to Chicago. His tenure as coach included 127 victories and spawned a legendary “Saturday Night Live” comedy sketch in which “Bill Swerski’s Superfans” laud all things to do with “Da Bears” and Ditka.

He parlayed his popularity into a wealth of ventures: restaurant owner, TV personality, co-owner of an Arena Football League team.

He once promoted his own brand of sausages and a line of wine and cigars.

Ditka’s folk-hero status belied a ruthless streak. Tough as nails, he was back on the sidelines a week after suffering a heart attack in 1988 — and he expected the same resolve from players.

Dave Duerson, a standout safety on the ’85 Bears team who was found to have the concussion-related brain disease CTE after he committed suicide in 2011, once said that Ditka “was not one who gave a damn about the players or their injuries when he was coaching.”

Ditka sparked controversy in 2017 when he weighed in against the national anthem protests led by quarterback Colin Kaepernick.

He never shied away from the spotlight, continuing to follow — and comment on — the Bears after a stroke in 2012 and another heart attack in 2018.

“I’m a Bears fan,” he said in December 2018. “Always will be.”

World.title: 'Our Gen Z deserves better than Emer-GenZ': Shashi Tharoor slams 'war-like deployment' of cops for CJP protest

NEW DELHI: Congress MP

on Saturday criticised the heavy security deployment across Delhi in the wake of Cockroach Janta Partyâs (CJP) protest against the

In a post, Tharoor said he had returned to the national capital after 2am and had ârarely seen anything likeâ the situation unfolding in Delhi, citing checkpoints, concrete barriers, spike strips, the deployment of 22,000 police and paramilitary personnel, cancellation of 250 trains and closure of 45 metro stations. He also referred to reports of young people being detained from their homes and streets in and around Delhi.

Tharoor criticised the suspension of internet services in central Delhi, calling it the âmost regressive (as well as repressive)â measure. He said freedom of movement had been âcompletely shackledâ and pointed out that Jantar Mantar had been designated as a place where citizens could voice dissent in the heart of the capital.

âOne is entitled to ask where this extraordinary manpower and urgency disappear when women in our capital need protection,â he said.





Questioning what would happen if protesters returned on Monday, Tharoor said those detained would have to be released. âOur GenZ deserves better than an undeclared Emer-GenZ,â he added.

Tharoor argued that a government confident in the fairness of elections should welcome questions about the electoral process rather than respond with heavy security measures. âThe government should provide answers, not lathis; expression, not repression,â he said.

He also said barricades would not restore public faith in the Election Commission and urged the poll body to answer questions raised by citizens. Calling the situation âutterly shameful and unconscionableâ, Tharoor said a democracyâs strength was measured by how it treated those who questioned its functioning.

World.title: Who will lead CJP protest? Abhijeet Dipke names Ajinkya Shinde in pre-recorded video

NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) on Saturday named its organisation in-charge Ajinkya Shinde to lead its protest at Jantar Mantar in New Delhi after founder Abhijeet Dipke, along with Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka, was detained by Delhi Police at the airport.

The development came as security was tightened across the national capital ahead of the CJP's proposed protest. Delhi Police had denied permission for the demonstration, citing law and order concerns and the possibility of inconvenience to residents.

Dipke had earlier said he was prepared to face arrest while travelling to Delhi for the protest. He accused Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union home minister Amit Shah of using security restrictions to prevent people from joining the demonstration.





Security tightened across Delhi

At least 1500 people had been detained under Section 65 of the Delhi Police Act as authorities stepped up security ahead of the planned demonstration.

Traffic restrictions came into force at 6 am, with diversions planned at several locations across the city. Police personnel were deployed at barricades and key intersections to check vehicles and monitor movement around the protest site.

World.title: What’s happening at Jantar Mantar? CJP’s ‘cockroaches’ grounded before anti-SIR showdown
World.content:
NEW DELHI: As planned, the âcockroachesâ could not make their way to Jantar Mantar, with the detention of key Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leaders before they could reach the protest site throwing the outfitâs âJantar Mantar 2.0â plans into disarray.

Delhiâs sweeping security crackdown, which has reportedly led to over 1,500 detentions across the capital, further dampened the expected turnout at the demonstration against chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.

CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke and leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka were detained by Delhi Police upon arriving at Indira Gandhi International airport from Mumbai.

The outfitâs head of legal affairs, Ratna Singh, was also detained.

The developments came hours before the outfitâs planned âJantar Mantar 2.0â demonstration demanding the removal of Gyanesh Kumar over the Election Commissionâs special intensive revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.

The protest, proposed by the CJP despite Delhi Police denying permission, was expected to draw around 20,000 participants. However, the detention of key organisers and the extensive security deployment have majorly affected preparations for the demonstration.





CJP leaders detained inside aircraft

In a video shared on social media, Dipke could be heard alleging that Delhi Police personnel entered the aircraft shortly after it landed to detain him and his fellow leaders.

âSo, you can see that Delhi Police is entering the plane to arrest us. They are all entering the plane. We just landed. All the Delhi Police officers are standing in the aisle. They are trying to arrest us from inside the plane. The entire Delhi Police is getting on the plane.

This is the fear of Narendra Modi,â Dipke said.

âNot even Indira Gandhi did this during the Emergency. All we wanted to do is a peaceful protest, and they are picking us up from the flight like we are criminals,â he added.

In the same video, CJP leaders Ranka and Das could be heard raising slogans of âBharat Mata Ki Jaiâ and âInquilab Zindabadâ.

The group termed the detentions "illegal" and alleged that the police action was aimed at preventing its leaders from reaching Jantar Mantar for the planned demonstration.

YouTuber Dhruv Rathee detained ahead of protest

Almost an hour before the CJP leadership arrived at Delhi airport, the outfitâs supporter and YouTuber Dhruv Rathee was reportedly detained by Gurugram Police from his residence in Sector 56.

Rathee, who lives abroad, had travelled to participate in the demonstration, according to the information shared by the outfit. His reported detention added to the uncertainty surrounding the protest, which had already triggered heightened security arrangements across Delhi and its adjoining areas.

35,000 personnel deployed; internet curbs & traffic restrictions

Delhi was placed under an extensive security blanket ahead of the proposed mobilisation. Around 35,000 police personnel were deployed, with Central Police personnel also present in large numbers around Jantar Mantar and other key locations.

The security arrangements included CCTV surveillance and body cameras fitted to the uniforms of deployed personnel.

A section of Delhi Police was also designated as the âPink Forceâ.

Mobile internet services were scheduled to be suspended within a 4-km radius of Jantar Mantar. Authorities also imposed traffic restrictions on roads along Delhiâs borders with Uttar Pradesh and Haryana, as well as routes leading to Jantar Mantar and other parts of New Delhi.

Police were coordinating with cab aggregators to regulate vehicle movement, while several trains were reportedly cancelled. The measures formed part of the broader security plan to manage the expected crowds and prevent disruptions across the capital.

The scale of the deployment, however, came amid allegations by the CJP that detaining its organisers before they could reach the venue was an attempt to prevent a peaceful protest.

Liquor shops shut, commercial activity affected

The restrictions extended beyond security and transport. Liquor outlets across Delhi were ordered to remain closed on October 9 and 10.

Commercial activity was also expected to be affected in parts of the city, particularly around Connaught Place.

Market associations in Connaught Place, Sadar Bazar and parts of Karol Bagh and Chandni Chowk confirmed closures for October 10.

Markets in Green Park, Sarojini Nagar and Greater Kailash, however, were expected to remain open.

The curbs and closures added to the disruption surrounding the proposed demonstration, with authorities preparing for a large turnout even as the detention of key organisers cast doubt on the protestâs eventual scale.

Rahul backs demand for CECâs removal, but Congress skips protest

Congress leader

reiterated his demand for Gyanesh Kumarâs removal, echoing the central demand of the CJP and other opposition voices opposing the SIR exercise.

In a post on X, the former Congress chief wrote: "Gyanesh Kumar will go. This government will go. "

"Then the repair of democracy will begin," he added, ending his post with the national flag emoji.

However, the Congress stayed away from the CJPâs planned demonstration.

Rahul travelled to Chennai to attend an event involving his ally and Tamil Nadu chief minister Vijay.

Former Delhi chief minister

, meanwhile, had promised to attend the protest with his family. But the detention of key CJP leaders and the heavy security deployment threatened to reduce the gathering well below the turnout initially anticipated by organisers.

Kejriwal criticised the Narendra Modi-led Centre over the restrictions, saying: âThis is worse than the Emergency, we are living under an absolute dictatorship ruled by Modi.â

CJP appeals for peace amid police restrictions

On the day of its planned âJantar Mantar 2.0â protest, the CJP issued an appeal urging participants to maintain peace, avoid violence and vandalism, follow lawful instructions and ensure that emergency services were not obstructed.

The outfit also called on participants to remain peaceful, alert and united. It described the demonstration as an effort to seek accountability over the Election Commissionâs special intensive revision of electoral rolls.

World.title: ‘Nuclear weapons not routine instruments of statecraft’: India’s warning to Pakistan at UN
World.content:
âIndia will not bow to nuclear blackmailâ: New Delhi hits back at Pakistan at UN (Anmol Sher Singh Bedi)

India reiterates three red lines

India raises Indus Waters Treaty, nuclear proliferation

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: India on Friday warned Pakistan against using nuclear weapons as a tool of political pressure, asserting that New Delhi would not bow to nuclear blackmail and that any terrorist attack against the country would invite a fitting response.Exercising its Right of Reply at the United Nations General Assembly's First Committee, which deals with disarmament and international security, India said nuclear weapons must not be treated as âroutine instruments of statecraftâ.Senior Adviser (Disarmament) at India's Permanent Mission to the Conference on Disarmament in Geneva, Anmol Sher Singh Bedi, delivered the response following remarks by Pakistan on Jammu and Kashmir.âJammu and Kashmir is an integral and inalienable part of India,â Bedi said, rejecting Pakistan's claims over the region.He said India's military capabilities were defensive in nature and shaped by its security environment, rather than directed against any particular country.âWe heard concerns about escalation. These are legitimate concerns. However, these are best judged by conduct over time. Nuclear weapons must not be treated as routine instruments of statecraft,â Bedi said.He warned that relying on the threat of nuclear weapons to shield activities below the threshold of conventional warfare could increase the risk of escalation rather than promote restraint.âA posture that relies on nuclear overhang to limit the consequences of subconventional activity raises the risk of escalation and not the prospect of restraint,â he said.Bedi also outlined what he described as a recurring pattern in regional crises, involving provocation, denial of responsibility and subsequent appeals for restraint after a response.âWhere those in power are neither elected by people nor accountable to them, their decisions carry no risk and impose no cost for those who take them. That is how crisis becomes an instrument of power. That is how instability becomes useful, and that is how the cycle keeps on repeating,â he said.India said its position on terrorism and national security remained clear, identifying three principles that would guide its response to threats.âFirst, any terrorist attack against India will receive a fitting response. Second, India will not bow to nuclear blackmail. Third, India will make no distinction between those who sponsor terrorism and those who mastermind it,â Bedi said.He said India's actions in May 2025 followed a âgrave provocationâ and were undertaken in self-defence after the April 22 Pahalgam terror attack in Jammu and Kashmir, in which 26 civilians, mostly tourists, were killed.âThese actions were measured, targeted, and designed to be non-escalatory,â Bedi said.India launched Operation Sindoor on May 7, 2025, targeting what it described as terrorist infrastructure in Pakistan and Pakistan-occupied Kashmir in retaliation for the Pahalgam attack. The Resistance Front, a proxy of Pakistan-based Lashkar-e-Taiba, was linked to the attack.Bedi also stressed that the use of non-state actors by a country did not absolve it of responsibility for their actions.âThe use of force by states under the garb of non-state actors does not erase the state's responsibility. India's right of self-defense remains intact,â he said.India also referred to the Indus Waters Treaty, arguing that the agreement depended on mutual trust and cooperation between the two countries.âA state cannot undermine those foundations of trust and cooperation and at the same time insist that the privileges flowing from the relationship remain untouched,â Bedi said.Following the Pahalgam attack, India announced that the treaty would be held in abeyance until Pakistan credibly and irrevocably ended its support for cross-border and other forms of terrorism.On nuclear proliferation, Bedi invoked the legacy of Pakistani nuclear scientist Abdul Qadeer Khan and the international proliferation network associated with him, which supplied nuclear equipment and expertise to countries seeking to develop nuclear weapons.The network contributed to international concerns that led to United Nations Security Council Resolution 1540, adopted in 2004, which requires states to prevent the proliferation of weapons of mass destruction and their means of delivery to non-state actors.âThis is relevant in the context of demands for unquestioned nuclear cooperation and transfer of advanced weapons and military capabilities. We urge all states and all responsible suppliers to exercise the highest degree of vigilance, not because of India, but for their own security,â Bedi said.

World.title: Detained! How CJP demonstration is being curtailed even before it started
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Hours before the Cockroach Janta Partyâs (CJP) planned demonstration could begin on Saturday, police action against its leaders and supporters was already under way, with multiple detentions across Delhi and beyond.

CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke, co-convenor Saurav Das and party leader Ashutosh Ranka were detained from inside the flight after the Mumbai flight landed.

Dhruv Rathee was also detained at his Gurugram residence, while CJP legal team head Ratna Singh alleged that she and three other lawyers had been detained ahead of the protest.

Police also detained people attempting to reach the Jantar Mantar, with reports of action near Janpath and other parts of the capital.

Over 1,600 detained

Over 1600 people have been detained across Delhi as a preventive measure ahead of the CJP protest, as authorities stepped up security and moved to prevent the gathering from taking place.

More than 400 members of the Students' Federation of India (SFI) were detained in Delhi on Saturday after they began marching towards Jantar Mantar around 10 am, SFI national president Adarsh M Saji told PTI.

SFI also alleged that police personnel visited HKS Surjeet Bhawan on Friday night to search for people planning to attend the protest.





The building houses the SFI Central Executive Committee office.

Several lawyers marching from the Supreme Court towards Jantar Mantar were also detained on Bhagwan Das Road after being stopped at police barricades. The protesters raised slogans and carried posters demanding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation. A lawyer said police had allowed them to march for around 100 yards before stopping them.

CPI(M) general secretary M A Baby, senior party leader Brinda Karat and other CPI(M) leaders were also detained at Jantar Mantar amid the police action against protesters.

Separately, Tushar Gandhi, great-grandson of Mahatma Gandhi, was detained ahead of a protest in Mumbai in support of the CJP's agitation at Jantar Mantar, extending the demonstrations and police action beyond the national capital.

The crackdown also extended beyond the national capital, with people travelling to Delhi for the demonstration reportedly intercepted at railway stations in Madhya Pradesh.

At least 14 students travelling from Pune were detained at Itarsi after being taken off the Goa Express on Friday.

Four CJP volunteers from Telangana had also been detained at Bhopal railway station on October 8 while travelling to Delhi for the protest.

The demonstration was called by CJP to demand the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.

Delhi Police had denied permission for the proposed gathering, citing security and procedural concerns.

The detentions and restrictions on movement have raised questions about the extent of preventive police action ahead of a planned demonstration.

The exact number of CJP supporters detained across Delhi and other states remains unclear, with reported figures covering different locations and categories of people.

CJP, student leaders condemn detentions

CJP condemned the detentions, calling them an attempt to prevent its leaders from joining the protest. Founder Abhijeet Dipke criticised the police action at Delhi airport, calling it âdictatorshipâ after he and two other party leaders were detained.

World.title: ‘I’m here to get arrested’: CJP chief Dipke’s prediction comes true at Delhi airport
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke and party leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka were detained by Delhi Police at the Indira Gandhi International Airport on Saturday, ahead of the partyâs proposed protest against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.

As he was getting detained, Dipke said, âEven Indra Gandhi didn't do this,â adding that âarrest hone liye hi aaya hu.â

Dipke had predicted his arrest, having earlier said that he was prepared to face detention as he was heading to Delhi for the October 10 protest.

Accusing Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union Home Minister Amit Shah of using security restrictions to prevent people from joining the demonstration, he had said he would not be deterred from fighting for free and fair elections.

"I wonder why the Prime Minister of this country is so afraid of the nation's youth and its people. What was the need to shut down all railway services? What was the need to halt all metro operations? They have cut off the internet and blocked the roads. They have brought the Army from J&K and deployed it in Delhi. They have summoned CRPF forces from Naxal-affected areas and deployed them in Delhi. Do Narendra Modi and Amit Shah want to wage war against the people of their own country? Is Gyanesh Kumar so dear to them that they would unleash their police and army forces upon their own citizens?"

Dipke alleged that the government feared a public backlash and was taking steps to discourage people from joining the protest.





"PM Modi is afraid; he fears that the people of this country will not vote for him after this. That is why, simply to cling to power, they are picking people up from trains. Announcements are being made in societies warning people not to join the protests. The Delhi Police is visiting homes, telling people not to participate in protests. But why shouldn't we? Protesting is our fundamental right. Article 19 grants us the fundamental right to protest in a democratic and peaceful manner, and that is exactly what we intend to do.

"

When asked whether he expected to be arrested upon reaching Delhi airport, Dipke said he was ready to face any action and would continue the fight for electoral reforms.

World.title: J&K regional parties join anti-CEC protests in Kashmir; Mehbooba, Omar liken Delhi situation to Kashmir of 2019
World.content:
Jammu & Kashmir’s regional parties, the ruling National Conference (NC) and the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), on Saturday (October 10, 2026) joined Congress-led protests in Kashmir at the call of the INDIA bloc, which is seeking the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar over the alleged voter list fraud. Meanwhile, J&K Chief Minister Omar Abdullah and PDP chief Mehbooba Mufti likened the security restrictions in Delhi with that of Kashmir of 2019.

Also Read: Anti-CEC Delhi protest updates on October 10

Carrying their party flags, dozens of NC and PDP workers, including women, assembled at the Congress party headquarters in Srinagar. The workers’ attempt to march on the streets of Lal Chowk was disallowed by the security forces. The protesters were carrying placards of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and CEC Kumar. They were demanding the resignation of the CEC over what they described as “vote chori” (vote theft).

Joint protests by the INDIA bloc parties were also held in central Kashmir’s Ganderbal and south Kashmir’s Anantnag.

“Workers of the NC, PDP and CPI(M) are jointly and peacefully holding a protest. We seek an inquiry into the functioning of CEC Kumar and his resignation. Those responsible for vote theft should face the law. Also, we stand with the leaders at the national level,” said Gayas Ahmad, a protester in Ganderbal.

Kashmir model has been exported to Delhi. Welcome to the New Delhi, modelled on New Jammu & Kashmir. — Omar Abdullah (@OmarAbdullah) October 9, 2026

As Delhi witnessed a security clampdown and internet shutdown ahead of the protests on Friday (October 9), J&K CM Abdullah, in a post on X, likened it to the situation in Kashmir in 2019, when the Centre ended the region’s special status. “The Kashmir model has been exported to Delhi. Welcome to the New Delhi, modelled on New Jammu and Kashmir,” said Mr. Abdullah, in the post.

Commenting on the situation in Delhi, former J&K Chief Minister and PDP chief Ms. Mufti, in a post on X, said, “Today’s Delhi is a chilling reminder of Kashmir after the unconstitutional abrogation of Article 370. People were locked in their homes, the internet was shut down, and an entire region was placed under siege”.

She said the BJP then brazenly claimed that nobody had protested. “Today, with Delhi under siege, trains halted, and roads to Jantar Mantar sealed, they may repeat the same lie, claiming that nobody protested against Gyanesh Kumar. First crush the protest, then deny it ever happened. This is how enforced silence is passed off as consent,” said Ms. Mufti.

World.title: 76 Years of Matsya: How a Chennai restaurant keeps Udupi food traditions alive
World.content:
One sunny afternoon in October, we step into Matsya Restaurant, where the cosy interiors and friendly staff immediately make us feel at home. We order our favourites from the menu — items that have not changed in years — rasa vada and chilli cheese toast.

As we wait for our order, Ram Bhat, a partner in the family-run establishment, walks in.

The establishment marks 76 years since its beginnings as an Udupi home and the occasion is prompting the family running the restaurant to look back at its roots and bring its heritage menu back into focus. “We want the current generation to enjoy the Udupi fare that we are known for,” says Ram, before insisting that we try their ven pongal served with fruit pachadi.

The combination does not particularly appeal to me at first, but I end up relishing the rather unusual pairing. “This is typical Udupi style. The fruit pachadi is made using fresh curd, and it is beaten with sugar. A mix of cut fruits is then added and served along with steaming-hot pongal,” he explains. The restaurant is also introducing tomato uthappam and apple bajji as part of its renewed focus on traditional offerings.

These new dishes make us wonder what Matsya might have looked like when it first began. What is its origin story? Ram Bhat answers.

Humble beginnings

Matsya’s history began long before the restaurant acquired its present name. It was originally known as Udupi Home, launched in 1950 by Ram’s father’s elder brother Shaama Bhat. . In 1980, his younger brother, Hari Bhat, rebranded the restaurant as Matsya, while retaining the ‘Udupi Home’ name for the boarding and lodging facility.

“My uncle started Udupi Home soon after I Independence. Our USP was its proximity to Egmore Railway Station, as well as several major hospitals and Government offices, all within a two-kilometre radius. In those days, people from the Udupi and Mangalore regions would come to Chennai and stay at our lodging. They would eat at the restaurant serving familiar food functioning on the ground floor, go about their business in the city, and then take the train back to their hometowns,” recalls Ram.

Over the years, the restaurant gained a loyal following for its vegetarian fare rooted in the culinary traditions of Udupi. But Matsya’s history is also closely intertwined with the changing rhythms of Chennai.

In 1962, during the India-China war, frequent blackouts were imposed across the city. It was during this period that the restaurant began serving food well past midnight — a tradition that continues to this day.

“We started serving idlis and filter coffee until 2am in those days, and the tradition continues even today. On our midnight menu, the most popular items are chilli cheese toast, bread peas masala, Udupi-style dosa, and filter coffee,” says Ram. As lifestyles changed, so did the late-night clientele. “We cater to those who go clubbing until the wee hours and also those who walk in after watching late-night film shows,” he adds.

The midnight menu is perhaps one of the clearest examples of how Matsya has adapted to the city around it while retaining its culinary identity.

Interestingly, Matsya has several feathers in its cap. It was among the early restaurants in the city to have a separate air-conditioned section, and by 1992, the entire restaurant had been air-conditioned. When Hari Bhat launched Matsya in 1980, he commissioned architect K Ramanan, who had designed Adyar Gate Hotel, later known as Crowne Plaza, to design the restaurant.

“It was the city’s elite who patronised us. The late Tamil Nadu Chief Minister MG Ramachandran would often order badam kheer from our kitchen whenever he hosted a party at his residence. RM Veerappan (politician), actor Nagesh, Cho Ramaswamy (political commentator and actor) and several other politicians also frequented the restaurant,” says Ram. The clientele may have changed over the decades, but Matsya has continued to evolve with it.

What’s changed?

When Ram and Shaama Bhat’s son, Prasad Bhat, took over the running of the restaurant in 1992, they revamped the menu to cater to a younger audience and the growing number of office-goers who began dropping in for lunch.

“We introduced dishes from the tandoor based on popular demand. I also launched the cold coffee, falooda and the Udupi thali, as I wanted to showcase the regional cuisine of the place I hail from, which is Dandathirtha near Udupi, and we also have lands in Moodibidri near Putthige. . In those days, an authentic Udupi thali was a rarity, and that was when our rasa vada became a rage among regular customers,” says Ram. F

At Matsya, the people behind the food have also traditionally reflected on its regional roots. Cooks have been sourced from the region, helpers have largely come from the southern parts of Tamil Nadu, while managerial staff have mostly been from the Tirunelveli region. The tradition continues even today.

The restaurant’s food has also found a wide audience since the pandemic, particularly its rasam. “During the lockdown and the pandemic, we made gallons and gallons of rasam. While we would normally prepare two cauldrons of rasam a day, during the pandemic years we were preparing six cauldrons,” says Ram.

Back to the basics

Today, Matsya is once again looking towards its heritage. The focus is on bringing traditional Udupi fare to the forefront and introducing diners to dishes that may not be as familiar as the ubiquitous dosa, Mangalore buns, and goli baje.

The menu now highlights specialities such as ragi dosa, jowar dosa, and thatte idli, alongside the more familiar Udupi favourites. The dessert selection, too, draws from the traditional recipes of Udupi and coastal Karnataka. The restaurant plans to introduce kuku rasayana, also known as mambala or mango payasam, a traditional no-cook Udupi summer dessert made with ripe mangoes, fresh coconut milk, and jaggery.

Other planned additions include halbai, a rice-and-jaggery-based sweet from coastal Karnataka; holige or obbattu, a sweet flatbread made with a soft outer dough and a filling of lentils and jaggery; and hyagreeva maddige, a popular temple offering from the Udupi region made with chana dal, jaggery, coconut and ghee.

The idea is not to turn back the clock, but to ensure that these dishes are not forgotten. “We have continued the Udupi legacy for three generations and hope to carry the tradition forward. Some of the Udupi snacks that were served only between 3pm and 7pm will now be available from noon to 7pm. We have been adapting and changing our menu to suit the generations we cater to, but Udupi fare will remain the highlight,” says Ram.

After 75 years, Matsya may have changed with its customers, its city and its times. But at its heart, the restaurant remains what it set out to be — a place where the flavours of Udupi have found a lasting home in Chennai.

World.title: Mumbai police detain Tushar Gandhi ahead of city’s anti-CEC protest
World.content:
Mumbai police detained Tushar Gandhi, president of Hum Bharat Ke Log, and a few other organisers of the Mumbai protest on Saturday (October 10, 2026). The detentions occurred ahead of a protest at August Kranti Maidan. The protest supported a demonstration by the Cockroach Janata Party at Jantar Mantar in Delhi.

Police picked up Mr. Gandhi at the National College intersection. Police took him to the DN Nagar police station.

#Watch | "We will continue our protest despite detention. We appeal to everyone to reach August Kranti Maidan this afternoon," said social activist Tushar Gandhi, who were allegedly detained by the Mumbai Police ahead of a protest in support of the anti-CEC protest in Delhi. Video: Special arrangement — The Hindu (@the_hindu) October 10, 2026

“We will continue our protest despite detention. We appeal to everyone to reach August Kranti Maidan today afternoon,” Tushar Gandhi and organisers said. The organisers said the police detained them.

Mr. Gandhi said that the police picked him up at the National College intersection. Initially, the police took him to Santa Cruz Police Station and later brought him to DN Nagar. He appealed; the protest continues. He said that he was in custody at DN Nagar Police Station. Mr. Gandhi said the police might take his phone. Organisers said that a few other leaders, including Feroze Mithoborewala, were also allegedly detained by the police.

The detentions occurred during a period of police vigilance across Maharashtra. Police in Mumbai and parts of the State tracked persons who intended to travel to Delhi. The Mumbai police detained more than 200 people on Friday (October 9, 2026) to stop them from leaving for the capital.

World.title: TVK’s bypoll victories a verdict on four months of good governance: Minister Arunraj
World.content:
Minister for Health, Medical Education and Family Welfare K.G. Arunraj on Saturday (October 10, 2026) described the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam’s (TVK)victories in the Dharapuram and Madurantakam Assembly byelections as a verdict on four months of good governance, and said more victories would follow.

Speaking to reporters after performing rituals for his ancestors in the Cauvery at Bhavani Kooduthurai on the occasion of Purattasi Mahalaya Amavasya, he said the TVK had won without distributing money or restricting voters, relying instead on the government’s achievements. He accused the DMK and the AIADMK of spreading false propaganda against the party.

Responding to DMK president M.K. Stalin’s description of the byelection results as “an interim victory for betrayal”, Mr. Arunraj said the people knew who had betrayed them. Rejecting the suggestion that the victory in Dharapuram was by a narrow margin, he claimed that the TVK had won without distributing money. He accused AIADMK general secretary Edappadi K. Palaniswami of betraying his party and claimed that AIADMK cadres had accepted the leadership of TVK president C. Joseph Vijay.

‘Dengue situation under control’

On dengue prevention, Mr. Arunraj said the situation was under control and there was no need for public apprehension. Adequate personnel had been deployed for mosquito-control operations, and facilities were available to treat patients who developed fever, he said.

On preparations for the Northeast monsoon, he alleged that the previous regime had claimed that 80% to 95% of stormwater drain works had been completed, but that the reality was different. The present government had taken up the works, and the Chief Minister had held three review meetings. He said the works were expected to be completed by the end of October, ahead of the monsoon.

‘Health workers should’ve submitted demands to govt.’

On the protest by mid-level health workers, Mr. Arunraj said they should have submitted their demands to him or the Health Department Secretary before resorting to agitation. He alleged that former DMK Minister Mano Thangaraj’s insistence on participating in the negotiations had delayed the talks. The workers had submitted a 21-point charter of demands, and the government had invited them for another round of discussions. Their demands would be resolved amicably, he said.

World.title: Anti-CEC Delhi protest LIVE updates: CJP's Ajinkya Shinde to lead protest; AISA shifts protest venue to Delhi Haat
World.content:
Even as the Delhi Police — who denied permission for the demonstration — detained founder Abhijeet Dipke and other CJP leaders including Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka as soon as they landed in Delhi, the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) said the youth protest will carry on with or without its leadership. Meanwhile, large number of protesters are being singled out, detained and taken away into buses from in and around the Jantar Mantar protest site in central Delhi.

The protest called by the CJP and other Left organisationson Saturday (October 10, 2026) looks to step up pressure on the demand of CEC Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation and the rollback of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. ”When the state uses mass detentions to silence democratic dissent, the public must take charge to save democracy,” the CJP statement read.

Also read | SC backs right to protest, says blanket transit ban in Delhi ‘over-reaching’

Earlier, YouTuber Dhruv Rathee was detained in a joint operation by the Delhi and Gurugram police from a residential flat in Gurugram on Saturday morning (October 10, 2026) and taken to an undisclosed location, according to sources in intelligence agencies.

Delhi Police expects around 7,000 protesters to arrive in the national capital, with senior officers directing personnel to exercise maximum restraint and handle the situation professionally, an official said.

Also read | Police send notices to students, CJP supporters ahead of October 10 Delhi protest

Authorities have taken several measures ahead of the protest, including internet curbs in parts of Delhi, the shutting down of markets and Metro stations, and the cancelling dozens of trains bound for the capital. The Union Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) directed all States and Union Territories (U.T.s) to coordinate with the Delhi Police and take preventive measures to stop the movement of protesters towards Delhi.

World.title: Five landmines found, defused along LoC in J&K’s Poonch
World.content:
Five landmines were detected and safely destroyed by the Army along the Line of Control (LoC) in Poonch district of Jammu and Kashmir, officials said on Saturday (October 10, 2026).

While two landmines were detected by an Army patrol party near the border fence in the Basoni top area on Saturday morning, three others had been found in the same area the previous day, the officials said.

They said the explosives were subsequently destroyed through controlled explosions by the Bomb Disposal Squad of the Army without causing any damage.

The forward areas along the LoC are dotted with landmines as part of an anti-infiltration obstacle system. However, heavy rainfall can sometimes wash away the mines, causing them to surface in areas where they may pose a potential risk.

World.title: No meat, big money: Inside India’s lucrative boom in upscale vegetarian dining
World.content:
Thirty-four years ago, three graduates of the Institute of Hotel Management in Chennai came together to launch Eden Vegetarian in Besant Nagar. Known for its Continental fare — corn florentine, crepes, milagu sevai shashlik, mushroom on toast — the restaurant is still packed with diners every day.

Venkatesh Balakrishnan, director, Eden Vegetarian, says upscale vegetarian restaurants in Chennai were a rarity when he launched the outpost with Aparna Venkatesh and Subadhra Raju. “We had Sangeetha and Saravanaa Bhavan serving traditional South Indian fare, but not Continental cuisine. Pasta, for instance, was only on five-star hotel menus,” says Venkatesh, adding that they wanted their focus to be on Italian and Continental fare. “People still come for our dishes like corn on toast, and Madras risotto that is made with basmati rice.”

After they opened, Venkatesh says they were overwhelmed with the response, and Eden was packed through the week with diners coming from as far as Broadway. In 2004, the trio launched a second outpost at Harrisons Hotel, which did well until a pandemic-induced closure.

The standalone vegetarian restaurant rises

While India has always had a strong vegetarian customer base, offerings like Eden Vegetarian were trendsetters for their time. Over the decades, the industry has seen several new dining formats, chefs exploring varied cuisines, and a shift in the way Indians eat out. But, a trend that has quietly been making its way across our culinary landscape is that of the standalone vegetarian restaurant.

Latest outposts include The Kind Roastery and Brew Roomz, Continuum in Bengaluru; Paashh, Uppu in Mumbai; among others. A study by Data For India says that the share of Indian adults who eat meat rose to 80% in 2021 from 74% in 2006 (dataforindia.com). Yet, vegetarian menus are clearly on the rise everywhere.

Highlighting Indian plants and produce

Four years ago, Rajan Sethi, managing director, Bright Hospitality, launched OMO, a farm-to-table kitchen in Gurugram to spotlight “India’s diversity of produce, regional food traditions, and culinary techniques”.

He says going all-vegetarian was a conscious decision. “The idea was never to create a vegetarian restaurant by simply removing meat from the equation. It was about building the entire experience around what we could do with plants and Indian produce,” he states, adding that their menu changes with the season.

Over the last two years, Rajan — who also runs Ikk Punjab in the capital — has seen vegetarian dining “move beyond being defined by what it excludes to being defined by what it can offer”.

He says guests are becoming more curious about vegetables like lingdu (fiddlehead fern), regional Indian ingredients such as Gobindobhog rice, and the stories behind what they eat. “There is a growing appetite for more thoughtful, ingredient-led vegetarian experiences. A lot of our diners are not necessarily vegetarian, but they are increasingly open to choosing a meal based on the ingredient and the experience rather than whether it includes meat,” Rajan adds.

What diners demand

Most often that not, when people think of vegetarian food, they automatically gravitate towards South Indian food, but this is slowly changing, says Deval Shah, founder of Mumbai-based Tao 66, which offers a seven-course vegetarian Thai tasting menu. “As long as the food is good and authentic, people aren’t necessarily looking at whether it is South Indian, North Indian, Asian, or anything else. Fusion was definitely a big trend for a long time, but people are now coming back to authentic, classic dishes with interesting ingredients,” he says.

For owner-Chef Niharika Peri of Bengaluru’s Eatinn’ Love Trattoria, the decision not to serve meat at her establishment was due to several factors, and not just that she is a vegetarian. The restaurant — known for its Neapolitan sourdough pizzas, pastas, and ice creams — is popular among communities such as Jains and Marwaris, who are more comfortable with an all vegetarian kitchen, she explains.

A new wave

In Bengaluru the concept of vegetarian fine-dining has been around longer than most cities. “1947 Restaurant was one of the pioneers in scaling up the fine-dining vegetarian space across multiple branches,” says Prem Vatsav of Eat Theory Hospitality who recently launched Alé (wave, in Kannada). “The London Curry House was a major trailblazer in introducing the innovative vegetarian concept to the city,” he adds.

Prem, who also helms Bangalore Brew Works (currently under renovation), says that “180% of our revenue here comes from liquor”. “Earlier, I would never consider launching a restaurant without a bar license, but there has been a shift in the industry. During research for Alé, we found that a majority of diners are willing to pay top dollar for truly innovative vegetarian dishes. We also recognised the large Jain population in the Jayanagar market, which prompted us to intentionally focus on providing extensive Jain options,” says Prem.

He secured a bungalow built in the 1960s with his architect wife, Arpita Jain, designing the space. “We preserved the structure entirely without breaking an inch of the house, choosing instead to utilise its courtyard where the 100-seater Alé sits.” The alleyway has been put to use as an all-day coffee and matcha bar, Co,Ma, serving specialty coffees, matcha, and eggless bakes.

Addressing the rise in non-vegetarians opting for vegetarian meals, Prem talks about how “most modern Indian restaurants thrive due to their innovative menus, driven heavily by social media influencer marketing, which has sparked curiosity among non-vegetarian diners as well”. Prem admits that the clientele at Alé is different from Bangalore Brew Works, where the focus was more on the alcohol. “In a concept like Alé, diners need more attention. We also value their suggestions, take feedback, and the concept is more food-centric,” says Prem.

Bakeries that skip eggs

And it is not just QSR’s or fine-dining establishments cashing in on the market, but bakeries and cloud kitchens too. Like Neha S Nirmal and Nischal Vasant Meethal’s Fillo Bakes, a vegetarian Japanese-inspired moving bakery that launched in the Garden City in December 2025. “For years, a large part of the vegetarian audience skipped baked goods because most contain eggs. I have also noticed that customers ask more about ingredients: butter or margarine, jaggery or millets, instead of how processed it is in terms of refined sugar and maida,” says Neha, who offers shokupans, milk breads, savoury karepans, and anpans.
